arbeitnow:head-of-technology-berlin-4673.description:
Fünf Praxen, ein Auftrag: Du verantwortest die Technik und baust Software, die unseren Teams Zeit zurückgibt. KU64 ist inhabergeführt, ohne Investoren und ohne Kette. Über 40 Zahnärztinnen und Zahnärzte arbeiten in fünf Praxen in Berlin und Potsdam, jeden Monat kommen über 1.000 neue Patientinnen und Patienten dazu.
Du verbindest IT-Betrieb und eigene Softwareentwicklung für alle fünf Standorte und berichtest direkt an die Geschäftsführung. Dabei arbeitest du mit den Praxisteams und unseren IT-Partnern zusammen, klärst Zuständigkeiten und entscheidest, was zuerst besser werden muss.
Das verantwortest du

• Betrieb an fünf Standorten: Netz, Server, Arbeitsplätze, Telefonie und Telematikinfrastruktur. Du sorgst für einen Betrieb, auf den sich jedes Team verlassen kann, und dafür, dass Wissen nicht nur in Köpfen steckt.

• Praxissoftware und Geräte: CGM Z1 Pro ist das Herz des Praxistags. Dazu digitales Röntgen, DVT, Intraoralscanner und CAD/CAM. Du koordinierst ihre Anbindung mit Teams, Herstellern und Partnern.

• Sicherheit und Datenschutz: Gesundheitsdaten verdienen Sorgfalt: Rechte, Verschlüsselung, Zwei-Faktor, Auftragsverarbeitung, Schulung. Und eine Wiederherstellung, die du geprobt hast.

• Partner und Budget: Du steuerst Dienstleister für Hardware, Telefonie und Gerätewartung, prüfst Verträge und machst Kosten und Prioritäten nachvollziehbar.

• Eigene Software und Agenten: Wir entwickeln unsere interne Software selbst, und sie wächst unter dir weiter. Du prüfst, wo KI-Agenten im Praxisalltag wirklich helfen, erprobst sie mit dem Team und bringst in den Betrieb, was sich bewährt.
Womit du arbeitest

• In der Praxis: CGM Z1 Pro, Doctolib, Personio, Telematikinfrastruktur

• Bildgebung und Geräte: DVT und digitales Röntgen, Intraoralscanner, CAD/CAM

• Infrastruktur: Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Windows Server, UniFi, Azure geplant

• Eigene Entwicklung: TypeScript, Cloud-Dienste, APIs und Schnittstellen, Sprachmodelle
Du musst nicht alles davon kennen.
Deine ersten 90 Tage

• 30 Tage, Verstehen: Du lernst Teams, Systeme und Verträge kennen und hältst fest, wo der Betrieb zuerst Aufmerksamkeit braucht.

• 60 Tage, Ordnen: Zuständigkeiten sind geklärt, die wichtigsten Verbesserungen laufen. Mit einem Team wählst du den ersten Anwendungsfall für einen Agenten.

• 90 Tage, Erproben: Deine Roadmap für die nächsten zwölf Monate liegt auf dem Tisch. Eine erste Lösung läuft im Praxisalltag, mit einem Menschen an ihrer Seite.
Das bringst du mit

• Du hast IT-Betrieb verantwortet: Für Systeme, Dienstleister und die Menschen, die damit arbeiten. Nicht nur für Code.

• Du entwickelst selbst: TypeScript, APIs und Cloud-Dienste. Du bringst Software zuverlässig in den Betrieb und hältst sie dort.

• Du nimmst Menschen mit: Du setzt Prioritäten und erklärst Technik so, dass ein Praxisteam sie gern benutzt. Deutsch fließend.
Ein Plus

• KI-Agenten oder Sprachmodelle im echten Einsatz

• CGM Z1 oder andere Praxis- und Kliniksoftware

• Telematikinfrastruktur, Röntgen und Medizingeräte im Netz

• Entra ID, Intune, Azure und UniFi
Das bieten wir

• Eine Rolle, die es noch nicht gab: Du baust sie auf und berichtest direkt an die Geschäftsführung.

• Wirkung, die man sieht: Was du baust, benutzen fünf Praxisteams am nächsten Morgen.

• Mittagessen im Haus: Unser Mitarbeiterrestaurant am Ku'damm.

• Büro am Kurfürstendamm 64: Mitten in der City West, mit dem Team im selben Haus.
So läuft die Bewerbung

• Bewerben: Ohne Anschreiben. Lebenslauf hochladen, fünf kurze Fragen beantworten und ein Beispiel aus deiner Arbeit beschreiben.

• Gespräch mit der Geschäftsführung: Am Ku'damm oder per Video. Wir reden über Systeme, die du verantwortet hast, und über das, was dich an der Rolle reizt.

• Ein Nachmittag im Haus: Du siehst Empfang, Behandlungszimmer und Technik und sprichst mit dem Team.

• Angebot: Wenn es passt, besprechen wir Gehalt und Starttermin.

As CTO & Co-Founder, you will own the technical direction of the company and the team that delivers it. You will lead an existing team of 3 engineers, grow it and set the standards for how it works.

We are building an AI-native engineering team from day one, with agentic engineering at the centre of how we write, review and ship code. Coding agents are not an add-on, but the default way we build software.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will stay close to the code while making the technical and organisational decisions that shape the company as it grows.

What You'll Do

• Lead and develop our existing team of 3 engineers, set high engineering standards and take ownership of what the team ships

• Own technical hiring and build the engineering organisation as the company grows

• Set the technical direction, from architecture and roadmap to build-vs-buy decisions

• Scale and operate reliable AI infrastructure, including APIs, cloud infrastructure, security, GDPR and European data residency

• Stay hands-on, writing code and contributing directly to our core systems

• Build an AI-native engineering culture where coding agents such as Claude Code are central to how the team develops, reviews and ships software

• Design and continuously improve our agentic engineering setup, from harnesses and workflows to orchestrating multiple agents in parallel, evaluating their output and benchmarking what works

• Represent the company technically with customers, in security reviews and in investor conversations

About You
You are an experienced technical leader who still loves to build. You have hired and led engineers, shipped complex systems into production and know how to make good technical decisions under real-world constraints.

You already work extensively with coding agents and have strong convictions about how AI is changing software engineering. You want to build a team around that approach, and you're excited by the ownership, ambition and uncertainty of becoming a co-founder.

• Proven experience leading, hiring and managing engineering teams, ideally in a startup, whether as a CTO, VP Engineering, Engineering Manager or Tech Lead

• Strong backend and platform foundations, including distributed systems, API design, cloud infrastructure and production systems

At Atlantic, we back founders in AI, compute, spacetech, and deep tech, often when it's still just a few people and a big idea. Why we are looking for you now
The breakthroughs we're most excited about will come from people who aren't on anyone's radar yet. We want to find them first and put them where they can have the biggest impact. arbeitnow:remote-senior-backend-engineer.title: Senior Backend Engineer (Go) (m/w/d)
arbeitnow:remote-senior-backend-engineer.description:
About us

As one of Germany's leading HealthTech companies, we are transforming discharge management by making it technology driven, patient centered, and free of bureaucracy. In addition to our market leading SaaS platform, we are developing AI solutions that radically simplify processes in clinics and for aftercare providers, relieve the burden on healthcare professionals, and put the focus back on patients. We currently connect over two thirds of all German hospitals with more than 650 rehabilitation clinics, and over 25,000 care and homecare providers. With around 120 employees from a broad range of nations, we are continuing to grow and are looking for people with the right attitude who want to improve the healthcare system alongside us.

We're now going far beyond our core business, aiming to eliminate bureaucracy and admin in hospitals with a whole portfolio of AI products.

What you'll work on

Aftercare provider operations are becoming increasingly complex and data driven. Bringing change is very hard, but we're not afraid. You'll build features that help care facilities, rehabilitation centers, and healthcare chains better allocate resources, unlock actionable insights from patient data, and integrate Recare seamlessly into their internal systems.
Our ambitious roadmap focuses on expanding our marketplace's receiver side with enhanced analytics tools, B2C platforms connecting providers directly with patients, expanded API integrations, and much more.
Secure communication is at our core. Our solution provides end to end encryption for healthcare professionals to safely exchange messages and patient data through both our applications and external API integrations.

In this role, you will:

• Own a domain inside our core Go codebase, contributing to architecture decisions and code quality within your area

• Work inside a well structured system with some standalone services around the edges, including an on premise gateway for hospital integrations, rather than a sprawling microservices estate

• Step in and keep things moving when your lead is away, taking ownership with confidence rather than waiting for instruction

• Contribute to pull requests, reviews, and technical discussions as a trusted senior voice on your team

We have several products in development that we are confident will significantly impact the German healthcare system. And yes, we're excited by the new opportunities AI unlocks for building powerful features for our customers and our own workflow.

What technologies you'll work with

• Golang. Our entire backend codebase is in Golang, and we love it. It's easy to learn, it's strongly typed, the internal tooling is fantastic, and it compiles fast.

• Postgres. We use Postgres for our databases and GORM to interface with it.

• CI and DevOps. We use both CircleCI and GitHub Actions to run our unit and integration tests, visual regression tests built in house, and automated code analysis through SonarCloud. They're also used to deploy to our various environments.

We also dedicate some of our time to work on non business tasks, which means for instance:

• Continuously optimising the backend code to offer the best user experience

• Analysing and improving database slowdowns and issues

• Internal automation, because we want to make our lives easier

• Building additional tooling, such as performance profiling tools to identify bottlenecks in backend services and optimise resource usage

Our philosophy is that developers are owners of the code they write until it gets to production. We rely a lot on automated tests to ensure everything stays stable. The rule is that code could be deployed at any time, and manual QA is only involved in new feature validation.

This is what you can expect from us

• Work with Purpose. Your work has a real impact on patients and healthcare professionals in the medical field.

• Corporate Culture. We embrace structures that foster high performance and strong team dynamics. Our interactions are characterized by mutual respect, loyalty, and recognition. We work together towards common goals and expect the same from you.

• Flexibility. Would you like to pick up your child from daycare? Do you enjoy exercising during lunchtime? We support you in achieving that balance. Besides flexible working hours, as a remote-first company we offer the flexibility to work 100% remotely from Germany, Spain, Portugal, Italy, Poland, France and Austria.

• Edenred card, which you can use in the way that suits you best.

• Extra Day Off on Your Birthday, so you can celebrate with your loved ones.

Your responsibilities as a Senior Backend Engineer will include

• Technical Ownership. Own a domain inside our Go codebase, contribute to architectural decisions and code quality within your area, identify bottlenecks and inefficiencies and suggest or implement improvements.

• Stepping Up When Needed. Be ready to take charge of priorities and keep things moving if your lead is away, supporting and mentoring other engineers along the way without needing to manage a team.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration. Work closely with product and design to translate business needs into technical solutions, and communicate technical progress, risks and trade-offs clearly.

• Delivery. Ship reliably against the team's roadmap, help break down features into deliverable tasks, and identify and remove blockers as they come up.

• Building With AI. We are an AI company now, and that shows up in how we expect people to work, not just what we build. Use AI tooling as a genuine part of your day to day, whether that is accelerating how you write and review code, prototyping ideas faster, or finding smarter ways to work. We do not expect you to vibe code everything end to end, plenty of our best engineers still want to write the core of what they ship themselves and use AI to speed things up around the edges. What matters is real curiosity about where this is heading, not scepticism about whether any of this changes how software gets built.

What you will need to succeed as a Senior Backend Engineer:

• We are looking for experienced developers. You have a CS degree or equivalent knowledge, and you have been coding full time professionally for 4 to 5 plus years

• We're looking for someone with production experience in Golang, or another C family language with a real, demonstrable ability to operate in Go without hand holding

• You have some experience supporting or mentoring other engineers, and you are looking for a strong individual contributor role rather than a path into people management

• You want to become a technical owner of part of our codebase. We need people who are looking for responsibility, just not a team to manage

• You are a clear, confident communicator, comfortable being put on the spot in a conversation and able to think out loud rather than defaulting to async only communication when something needs a real time answer

• Since Product and Engineering work in a fully remote setup, writing skills matter more and more, so written questions, requirements, and docs are genuinely valuable

• You should be comfortable and excited to dive into more advanced topics, for example build pipelines, caching mechanisms, and database optimisation

• Since we're a small team, we want to automate a lot. You should have experience with CI and testing frameworks

• You are proactive and proficient across the entire product development flow, asking questions, clarifying specs, raising doubts, and engaging in meetings

• Healthcare experience is a bonus, not a requirement. FHIR, HL7, or DICOM exposure is great to have, but we have hired strong engineers from fintech, insurtech, and other compliance heavy domains with zero healthcare background who did just fine

• You are genuinely excited about what AI can do for engineering. We don't expect every line of code to be AI generated, but we do expect curiosity and a real point of view on where this is heading

arbeitnow:remote-senior-data-engineer-be.title: Senior Data Engineer (m/f/d)
arbeitnow:remote-senior-data-engineer-be.description:
As one of the leading German HealthTech companies, we are reshaping discharge management – technology-driven, patient-centered, and free from bureaucracy. In addition to our market-leading SaaS platform, we develop AI solutions that radically simplify processes in hospitals and for aftercare providers, relieve healthcare professionals, and refocus attention on patients. Today, we already connect two-thirds of all German hospitals with over 650 rehabilitation clinics and 25,000 nursing and homecare providers. With currently around 100 employees, we continue to grow – and we are looking for people with character who want to help us improve the healthcare system and solve administrative complexity across care journeys in Europe.

Our data flows from our applications, product events and business systems, in a highly regulated healthcare context. This role exists to build the platform that makes sure that data arrives complete, on time and safe to use, so Product, leadership, RevOps and Finance work from the same numbers.

You will be the first data engineer in a new data team that sits in Product, works across the company and reports to the Head of Data. You will own the platform that moves our data into Snowflake and shape the architecture decisions around it: which tools we build on, how pipelines are orchestrated and monitored, and how data infrastructure is managed as code.

What to expect
This is what you can expect from us as a Senior Data Engineer:

• Purposeful work – your work gives the teams serving hospitals and aftercare providers data they can trust.

• Real ownership – as the first data engineer in a new team, you shape the data platform and its tooling.

• Company culture – we believe in flat hierarchies that promote high performance and strong team dynamics. We foster an environment characterized by mutual respect, loyalty, and recognition. Together, we strive for our goals – and expect the same from you.

• Flexibility – want to pick up your child from daycare? Like to exercise during lunch? We'll support you. We are a remote-friendly company offering flexible working hours. Workations are also possible by arrangement.

• Edenred card – which you can use according to your needs.

Extra vacation day – so you can celebrate your birthday with your loved ones, you'll have the day off.

This is how you will make an impact as a Senior Data Engineer:

• Data from our application databases, product events and SaaS tools needs to reach Snowflake reliably. You build and run that ingestion and decide where to buy a managed connector and where to build.

• Our pipelines need clear dependencies, retries, alerting and SLAs. You set up orchestration so a failed or partial load stops downstream work instead of silently producing wrong numbers.

• New products need event pipelines. You design them together with engineers, keeping patient data out of analytics events by design.

• Product and Finance need to work from the same definitions. You maintain the dbt models that connect product usage with customer, billing and revenue data.

• Our CRM (HubSpot) and our internal systems need to talk to each other. You build the data flows between them, including two-way synchronisation where it is needed.

• Data quality problems need to be caught before a dashboard or a board report does. You establish validation, monitoring and alerting.

• Our data needs strong privacy and access controls. You enforce role-based access and masking in Snowflake, pseudonymisation, and deletion that propagates across raw and modelled data.

• Data code needs the same engineering standards as our product code. You bring code review, testing, documentation and CI/CD to it.

How we build
We run a modern cloud-native stack to move, model and protect data reliably in a regulated healthcare environment.

• Cloud: AWS (The European Sovereign Cloud partition)

• Runtime: Kubernetes (EKS) and Postgres (RDS)

• Warehouse and modelling: Snowflake (EU), dbt

• Orchestration: Airflow or Dagster (being introduced)

• BI: Looker

• Observability: Datadog

• CI/CD: GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Actions

• Infrastructure: CloudFormation

• Business systems: HubSpot, Chargebee

• Several years (typically 5 or more) building production data pipelines, as a data engineer or as a backend engineer on data-intensive systems.

• Strong Python: you write tested, maintainable production code, not only scripts.

• Advanced SQL, including window functions, CTEs and query optimisation.

• Production experience with Snowflake or a comparable cloud warehouse: compute sizing and cost control, role-based access, masking, and performance tuning.

• Experience with dbt, or a similar tool for tested and documented transformations.

• Solid ingestion fundamentals: initial versus incremental loads, change data capture from Postgres, idempotency, schema evolution, late and out-of-order data, and backfills.

• Production experience with an orchestrator such as Airflow or Dagster.

• Experience with AWS and with deploying your own work in containers.

• A data quality mindset: you profile data, test assumptions and build checks.

• Practical knowledge of GDPR: you can identify personal data and implement pseudonymisation, access control and deletion.

• You use AI coding tools in your daily work and know where they help and where they need checking.

• Ability to own decisions as the only data engineer and to explain technical trade-offs to non-engineers.

• Preference for writing over talking, resulting in clear, concise, yet complete documentation and asynchronous communications.

• Fluent English, written and spoken. Other languages are a plus.

Bonus points

• Healthcare or regulated-domain experience (e.g. ISO 27001, C5).

• Integrating CRM and SaaS systems such as HubSpot or Salesforce, including reverse ETL or two-way sync.

• Designing product event tracking (e.g. Snowplow or Segment).

• Kubernetes in production.

• Reading and changing Go code.

• Managing Snowflake as code.

• German language skills.

Our values
This will help you decide if you want to join us – our values are:

• Strong opinions, weakly held. We adapt, negotiate trade-offs, and reconsider decisions when necessary. We don't stick to one implementation – we re-evaluate and adjust as needed (including throwing away the old one).

• Pragmatic choice of tools and avoidance of one-size-fits-all thinking.

• Bringing professionalism and empathy to how you work with others.

• Strong belief in solid technical fundamentals and preference for understanding and first principles over memorization.

RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works.
 
At RobCo, we automate the ordinary, so humans can do the extraordinary. To achieve this, we are looking for an ambitious Automation, IT Systems & Security Specialist (m/f/d) to help us establish RobCo as leading provider of automation solutions.
In this key role, you act as the architect and guardian of our internal IT infrastructure. Your focus is not on maintaining the status quo, but on building a highly secure, automated, and scalable system landscape. You eliminate manual effort through intelligent IT automation and ensure that our network and security architecture keeps pace with our global growth.

• Design and implementation of a secure, cloud-aligned IT and network landscape (e.g. AWS, Zero Trust principles)

• Ensuring highest standards in Identity & Access Management (IAM), SSO, and secrets management

• Protection of endpoints and continuous monitoring of system integrity across all teams

• Identification and automation of repetitive IT processes (e.g. automated onboarding/offboarding, asset management)

• Selection and integration of tools that connect and streamline internal workflows across Finance, HR, and Engineering

• Active use of modern automation tools, including AI-supported solutions, to sustainably reduce manual support effort

• Ownership of global device and lifecycle management, including rollout processes

• Acting as a technical lead for complex first- and second-level support topics

• Close collaboration with Engineering and Cloud teams on infrastructure, security, and automation topics

We're looking for someone who has:

• Completed vocational training or a degree in Computer Science, IT Systems, Security or a comparable field

• Several years of experience in system administration, network architecture, or IT security in cloud environments

• Strong ownership mindset: you take responsibility, proactively identify gaps, and close them independently

• A strong automation mindset: you are driven by the principle of not doing things twice manually and actively use scripting or tools to improve processes

• Deep understanding of cloud architectures, modern identity models, and network security concepts

• A structured and pragmatic working style, combined with a strong ownership mindset and focus on scalable systems

• Very good English skills (German is a plus)

Why join RobCo?

• Develop modular, software-defined robotics solutions with us that set new standards in automation.

• Help us build robots equipped with state-of-the-art AI that perceive their environment, analyze data, and make intelligent decisions in real time.

• As part of a very dynamic and fast-growing scale-up, you will take on responsibility from day one, drive your own projects, and see the direct impact of your work.

We solve our customers' most pressing pain points - labor shortage, cost pressure, workplace safety, and national reshoring - across the full spectrum of Autonomous Industrial Robotics. In October 2026, RobCo reached unicorn status with a valuation exceeding one billion US dollars, with its valuation doubling in less than nine months. arbeitnow:it-assistant-munich-261304.description:
About surge aero
At surge aero, we're a growing aerospace and defence technology company developing high-performance propulsion systems and advanced unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).
We're a team of curious, ambitious and hands-on people working on technology that pushes boundaries and makes a real impact in the aerospace and defence industry.
Based in Germany, we bring together people from different backgrounds who enjoy building things, solving problems, sharing ideas and getting things done. We value initiative, teamwork and a practical, can-do attitude.
We're growing and always excited to welcome new people who want to be part of the journey. It's a great opportunity to join an international-minded team, work on challenging technology and help shape what comes next.
Come join us and be part of building the future of aerospace and defence!
About the Role
We are looking for a motivated and hands-on IT Assistant to support our daily IT operations at our Heimstetten office.
In this role, you will provide first-level IT support to employees, assist with hardware and software management, and ensure that our workplace technology runs smoothly. You will work closely with the internal team to support onboarding, troubleshooting, and general IT administration.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a practical interest in IT, strong problem-solving skills, and a service-oriented mindset.

Key Responsibilities
IT Support & Troubleshooting

• Provide first-level IT support to employees for hardware, software, and connectivity issues.

• Troubleshoot laptops, desktops, monitors, printers, peripherals, and basic network issues.

• Assist employees with Microsoft 365 applications, Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint.

• Escalate complex technical issues to external IT providers or senior IT personnel when necessary.

Hardware & Equipment Management

• Order, prepare and configure laptops and workstations for new employees.

• Install and update software, operating systems, and security tools.

• Manage IT equipment inventory, including laptops, monitors, accessories, and peripherals.

• Coordinate hardware repairs, replacements, and technical maintenance.

Employee Onboarding & Offboarding

• Support the technical onboarding of new employees, including device preparation, account setup, and access configuration.

• Assist with account deactivation and equipment collection during offboarding.

• Ensure employees have the necessary IT equipment and access to perform their roles.

IT Administration & Security

• Maintain accurate IT asset records and documentation.

• Support basic IT security practices, including software updates, antivirus, and device compliance.

• Assist with user access management and password-related issues.

• Help maintain an organised and efficient IT environment.

Requirements

• Previous experience in IT support, IT administration, or a similar role is an advantage.

• Basic knowledge of Windows operating systems and Microsoft 365.

• Familiarity with computer hardware, software installation, and troubleshooting.

• Basic understanding of networking, Wi-Fi, and IT security.

• Strong problem-solving and communication skills.

• Ability to work independently and take a hands-on approach.

• Good command of English; German is an advantage.

• Currently based in or able to commute to Heimstetten, Germany.

What We Offer

• Part-time employment with flexible working arrangements.

• A hands-on role in an international and technology-driven company.

• Direct exposure to IT operations in an aerospace and engineering environment.

• A collaborative and international working environment.

• Opportunity to develop technical skills and grow with the company.

Work Location
This position is based onsite at our office in Heimstetten, Germany. Regular physical presence is required to provide direct support to employees and manage IT equipment.

Wer wir sind
EMPA ist eine Beratung für Data & Management Consulting mit Sitz in Frankfurt am Main. Im Bereich Financial Services unterstützen wir Banken, Asset Manager, Kapitalverwaltungsgesellschaften, Depotführer und Verwahrstellen dabei, ihr Geschäft weiterzuentwickeln, Abläufe zu verbessern und neue Lösungen einzuführen.
Bei uns bringst du deine Erfahrung und deine Ideen in Kundenprojekte ein. Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit deinem Team Lösungen und begleitest deren Umsetzung beim Kunden. Gleichzeitig hast du die Möglichkeit, eigene fachliche Schwerpunkte zu setzen, neue Beratungsangebote zu entwickeln und unseren Financial-Services-Bereich mit aufzubauen.
Deine Aufgaben

• Als (Senior) Consultant begleitest du unsere Kunden von der fachlichen Fragestellung bis zur Umsetzung. Je nach Projekt und Erfahrung arbeitest du als Business Analyst, Requirements Engineer, Scrum Master oder im PMO. Perspektivisch kannst du auch als (Teil-)Projektleiter oder Product Owner Verantwortung übernehmen.

• Du analysierst Abläufe im Banking, Asset Management und Depotgeschäft und entwickelst Vorschläge, wie sich diese verbessern lassen.

• Du übersetzt fachliche Fragestellungen in verständliche Konzepte und konkrete Anforderungen, die du mit Fachbereichen und IT abstimmst.

• Du gestaltest digitale Produkte und Onboarding-Prozesse mit und unterstützt die Weiterentwicklung von Plattformen und Schnittstellen.

• Du arbeitest an Daten- und KI-Vorhaben, verbesserst die Datenqualität und identifizierst Möglichkeiten zur Automatisierung.

• Du unterstützt unsere Kunden dabei, regulatorische Anforderungen in ihren Prozessen und Systemen umzusetzen.

• Du übernimmst Verantwortung für Arbeitspakete, führst Workshops durch und begleitest Tests sowie die Einführung neuer Lösungen.

• Du entwickelst mit uns Beratungsangebote, Methoden und Fachbeiträge und bringst dein Wissen in Kundengespräche ein.
Das bringst du mit

• Du hast ein Studium der Wirtschaftswissenschaften, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Informatik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung abgeschlossen oder verfügst über eine entsprechende berufliche Qualifikation.

• Du bringst erste oder mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Banking oder Asset Management mit – aus einer Linienfunktion bei einem Finanzinstitut oder aus Beratungsprojekten für Banken, Asset Manager oder andere Finanzdienstleister.

• Du kennst dich in mindestens einem unserer Themenfelder aus – Depotgeschäft, Investment Operations, digitale Plattformen, Datenmanagement oder Projektsteuerung.

• Du hast Erfahrung im fachlichen Test, etwa bei der Erstellung von Testfällen, der Durchführung von Tests oder der Dokumentation und Nachverfolgung von Fehlern.

• Du arbeitest dich zügig in neue Themen ein, erkennst Zusammenhänge und kannst komplexe Sachverhalte verständlich erklären.

• Du arbeitest selbstständig, stimmst dich mit deinem Team ab und bringst eigene Vorschläge ein.

• Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutsch- und gute Englischkenntnisse und bist bereit, abhängig vom Projekt auch vor Ort bei unseren Kunden zu arbeiten.
Erfahrung mit Atlassian-Tools wie Jira und Confluence sowie ALM Octane ist willkommen. Zusätzliche Pluspunkte sind Kenntnisse in BPMN, SQL oder Power BI. Wünschenswert sind Zertifizierungen in Scrum, PRINCE2, Requirements Engineering oder im Softwaretest, etwa ISTQB Certified Tester Foundation Level (CTFL) oder ISTQB Certified Tester Acceptance Testing (CT-AcT).
Was wir dir bieten

• Anspruchsvolle Kundenprojekte, in denen du Lösungen von der Konzeption bis zur Einführung begleiten kannst.

• Die Möglichkeit, neue Beratungsangebote mitzuentwickeln und beim Ausbau unseres Financial-Services-Bereichs Verantwortung zu übernehmen.

• Schulungen und Weiterbildung, mit denen du dein Wissen vertiefen und neue fachliche Schwerpunkte erschließen kannst.

• Ein Team, das Erfahrungen teilt, gemeinsam an Lösungen arbeitet und sich gegenseitig unterstützt.

• Eine attraktive Vergütung, die deine Erfahrung und deine Fähigkeiten berücksichtigt.

• Moderne Ausstattung, ein zentral gelegenes Büro in Frankfurt, regelmäßige Teamevents und eine Wellpass-Mitgliedschaft.
Dein nächster Schritt
Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen. Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und deinen möglichen Eintrittstermin. Gemeinsam besprechen wir, ob der Einstieg als Consultant oder Senior Consultant zu deiner Erfahrung passt.

arbeitnow:head-of-finance-finanzleiter-f.description:
Deine Aufgaben

1. Kaufmännische Gesamtverantwortung

• Sie übernehmen die operative Steuerung der Finanz- und Rechnungswesenprozesse unserer Immobilien- und Projektgesellschaften.

• Sie stellen die ordnungsgemäße und termingerechte Erstellung der Jahresabschlüsse sicher und steuern die Zusammenarbeit mit Steuerberatern und Wirtschaftsprüfern.

• Sie verantworten Liquiditätsplanung, Zahlungsverkehr, Budgetierung und kaufmännisches Controlling.

• Sie entwickeln ein aussagekräftiges monatliches Reporting über Gesellschaften, Immobilien und Projekte.

• Sie schaffen Transparenz über Kosten, Erträge, Verbindlichkeiten und wirtschaftliche Risiken.

2. Immobiliencontrolling und Nebenkosten

• Sie verantworten die kaufmännische Kontrolle unserer Immobilienbestände und Mietverhältnisse.

• Sie prüfen die bereits teilweise automatisiert erstellten Nebenkostenabrechnungen auf rechnerische, vertragliche und wirtschaftliche Richtigkeit.

• Sie kontrollieren Umlageschlüssel, Kostenpositionen, Mietvertragsregelungen und Abweichungen.

• Sie stellen die Qualität der Abrechnungen sicher und entwickeln die bestehenden Prüf- und Freigabeprozesse weiter.

• Sie identifizieren Fehlerquellen und sorgen für dauerhaft zuverlässige Abläufe.

3. Finanzierung und Transaktionen

• Sie betreuen unsere bestehenden Bankverbindungen und koordinieren laufende Immobilienfinanzierungen.

• Sie strukturieren gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung neue Finanzierungen für Bestandsimmobilien, Projektentwicklungen und Immobilienankäufe.

• Sie erstellen und prüfen Finanzierungsmodelle, Wirtschaftlichkeitsrechnungen und Investitionskalkulationen.

• Sie überwachen Kreditbedingungen, Covenants, Zinsbindungen und Finanzierungstermine.

• Sie begleiten Immobilientransaktionen von der wirtschaftlichen Prüfung bis zur Umsetzung.

4. Digitalisierung und KI-Automatisierung

Ein wesentlicher Bestandteil Ihrer Aufgabe ist die kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung unserer Finanzorganisation.

• Sie analysieren bestehende Prozesse und identifizieren konkrete Automatisierungspotenziale.

• Sie optimieren die digitale Verarbeitung von Rechnungen, Buchhaltungsdaten, Mietverträgen und Nebenkostenabrechnungen.

• Sie entwickeln automatisierte Kontrollmechanismen, Berichte und Workflows.

• Sie setzen KI-Anwendungen dort ein, wo sie Qualität, Geschwindigkeit und Wirtschaftlichkeit messbar verbessern.

• Sie sorgen für eine zuverlässige Integration bestehender Softwarelösungen und Datenquellen.

• Sie reduzieren manuelle Routinetätigkeiten und schaffen Freiräume für wertschöpfende Aufgaben.

Dein Profil

• Sie haben ein abgeschlossenes betriebswirtschaftliches Studium mit dem Schwerpunkt Finanzen

• Oder: Sie haben eine kaufmännische Ausbildung absolviert, idealerweise mit einer Zusatzqualifikation als Bilanzbuchhalter*in.

• Sie bringen einschlägige Erfahrung im Finanzbereich mit, idealerweise als Buchhalter*in in Start-ups oder in der Immobilienbranche.

• Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse.

• Sehr gute numerische Fähigkeiten und hohe Detailgenauigkeit.

Was wir Dir bieten

• 24 Urlaubstage pro Jahr und ein attraktives Gehalt.

• Flexible Arbeitszeiten nach einem Gleitzeitmodell.

• Ein multikulturelles Team mit flachen Hierarchien und viel Raum für neue Ideen.

• Ein offenes und helles Büro mit Snacks und Getränken.

• Die Möglichkeit, dich in neuen Arbeitsbereichen einzuarbeiten und mehr Verantwortung zu übernehmen.

• Regelmäßige Firmenveranstaltungen und Meetings, bei denen alle zusammenkommen, um Erfolge zu feiern und voneinander zu lernen.

Ein Betrieb läuft mit SO'USE, das Terminal funktioniert, die Gäste bestellen selbst. Und dann? Genau da setzt du an - schlägst noch die Anbindung der Lieferdienste und den eigenen Webshop vor. Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere Bestandskunden das volle Potenzial unserer Plattform nutzen, und machst aus zufriedenen Kunden Betriebe, die mit uns wachsen.
SO'USE ist eine Plattform für digitales Bestellen und Bezahlen in der Gastronomie. Gäste scannen einen QR-Code oder tippen am Self-Order-Terminal, bestellen selbst und zahlen direkt – die Bestellung landet ohne Umweg in der Kasse und auf dem Küchendisplay. Dazu kommen Webshop, Tablet-Bestellung und die Anbindung von Lieferdiensten wie Lieferando, Wolt und Uber Eats. Über 1.500 Betriebe arbeiten damit täglich: vom Foodtruck über Bäckereiketten bis zu HANS IM GLÜCK.
Was du bei uns machst

• Du betreust unsere Bestandskunden aktiv, vor allem am Telefon und in MS-Teams-Calls, und suchst den Kontakt, bevor Probleme entstehen.

• Dein Ziel: Kunden nutzen das volle Produktportfolio von SO'USE, vom Self-Order-Terminal über Webshop und Tablet-Bestellung bis zur Lieferdienst-Anbindung.

• Du wirkst durch Schulungen oder weitere Produkte darauf hin, dass möglichst viele Bestellungen per Onlinezahlung abgewickelt werden, und zeigst Betrieben, welchen Mehrwert das für sie hat.

• Der Bereich ist im Aufbau. Du findest proaktiv Aufgaben, entwickelst Prozesse und Vorgehensweisen mit und gibst Kundenfeedback an das Produktteam weiter.

• Du nutzt KI-Tools, um Kundenkommunikation, Auswertungen und deine Arbeitsabläufe effizienter zu gestalten.

Was du mitbringst

• Starke Kommunikation, besonders am Telefon und in MS-Teams-Calls. Du telefonierst gern und viel, auch mit Menschen, die gerade keine Zeit haben.

• Emotionale Intelligenz und Einfühlungsvermögen. Du kannst Kritik aushalten, Kunden beruhigen und Gespräche in eine konstruktive Richtung lenken.

• Proaktivität und Eigeninitiative. Du arbeitest gern selbstständig und packst Aufgaben an, bevor sie jemand verteilt.

• Gastro-Erfahrung! Du hast im Service, in der Küche, oder in der Betriebsleitung oder in gearbeitet und weißt, wie sich ein voller Laden anfühlt. Das hilft dir, Prozesse vor Ort zu verstehen.

• Keine Berührungsängste mit KI. Du bist offen für neue Tools und nutzt sie selbstverständlich.

• Schnelle Auffassungsgabe. Neue Produkte und Prozesse sind für dich der spannende Teil.

Von Vorteil, aber kein Muss:

• Erfahrung im Customer Success, Account Management oder Vertrieb, idealerweise in einem Gastrotech-Unternehmen

• Erfahrung mit Gastro-Kassensystemen

Was wir bieten

• Vergütung: Gesamtvergütung von 45.000 bis 60.000 Euro im Jahr, je nach Erfahrung und Zielerreichung. Sie setzt sich aus einem festen Gehalt und einem variablen Bonus zusammen.

• Perspektive: Wer bei uns Kunden und Produkt kennt, hat gute Chancen, den Bereich perspektivisch als Teamleitung zu entwickeln.

• Arbeitsplatz: Vorzugsweise in Leipzigs Mitte, aber auch remote möglich. Wir sitzen gern zusammen im Büro, aber wenn du von woanders arbeitest, funktioniert das auch.

• Arbeitskultur: Flexible Arbeitszeiten, flache Hierarchien und ein entspannter Umgang im Team.

• Entwicklung: Regelmäßiges Feedback und Workshops statt Jahresgespräch.

Klingt nach dir?
Dann schreib uns. Ein kurzes Motivationsschreiben und dein Lebenslauf reichen uns völlig. Erzähl uns gern, aus welchem Laden du kommst.
Fragen vorab? Melde dich einfach direkt, auch ohne fertige Bewerbung.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

What you'll do
The Release, Environments and Change Engineer (REC Engineer) has three key areas of responsibility. You will operate Release, Environments and Change processes and procedures, and you’ll be involved in, and often lead, the identification and implementation of process improvements using AI and other tools.
You will work closely with the REC Manager and Environments Manager and operate the processes they define. These processes may rely on manual activities and controls at first, so you’ll take a leading role in replacing them with appropriate automation, and then identify mechanisms and methods to govern those automated controls.
You will collaborate with Enablement teams and engineering teams across Kaluza to make sure processes are understood, embedded and followed. You’ll be a decision maker with the authority to decline or postpone releases and changes, and you’ll handle client communication where approval is required for a change or release.

• Operating promotion gates, making promote or block decisions between environments in line with contractual and ways-of-working agreements, and escalating high-risk calls.

• Facilitating change approvals, release Go/No-Go meetings and release trains, preparing releases against readiness criteria and tracking per-team readiness and environment-deployed status.

• Using AI-assisted checks to confirm quality gates are met, summarise what changed in a release, score change risk and flag incomplete or stale records, applying your own judgment to improve the reliability of the results.

• Maintaining complete, accurate change and configuration records, keeping every change traceable across the full environment stack, and managing the change and release calendar.

• Building and maintaining release automation, including readiness checks, artefact promotion, AI-drafted release notes and notifications, and reporting feeds.

• Working with engineering teams in real time to roll back failed releases or apply fixes, and coordinating with incident and problem management so planned changes, hotfixes and major incidents stay in sync.

• Communicating changes and releases internally and externally, supporting environment coordination and validation, running post-implementation reviews and retros, and giving operational input into gate definitions and the wider process.

What you’ll bring 

• Strong organisation and attention to detail, with the ability to juggle multiple moving parts and spot incomplete records or inconsistencies.

• Clear communication and strong facilitation skills, comfortable coordinating across teams, leading check-ins, keeping everyone aligned, driving decisions and chasing things through to completion.

• The confidence to say no and hold the line when something isn’t ready, and to escalate when you’re unsure.

• Comfort with Jira (or similar), including configuring boards, workflows and tickets.

• Scripting and automation skills to build and maintain the automation around a release process (readiness checks, artefact promotion, release notes and reporting), plus familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and integrating automated testing into deployment workflows.

• Day-to-day use of AI tooling with a critical eye, catching what it gets wrong rather than waving it through.

• Experience building or integrating AI agents (e.g. LangChain, AutoGen, custom frameworks, MCP-based tooling), with an understanding of prompt engineering and LLM evaluation techniques such as faithfulness, relevance and LLM-as-a-judge, since traditional pass/fail assertions don’t translate well to testing AI agents.

What will set you apart

• Any exposure to how software gets released or how environments work, even informally.

• Light scripting or automation experience, or the appetite to learn it.

• A calm head under time pressure.

About Kaluza
Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

The role
You’ll join the Kaluza Technology community: a large team of product-focused and data-led Product and Platform Engineers working at serious scale. Our ecosystem is diverse depending on the team, spanning TypeScript on AWS, Go on GCP, and Scala, so we care more about how you think through a problem than which language you learned it in. As a Software Engineer you’ll work in a product team on real features from your first weeks: shaping them with product and design, building them, shipping them, and learning to run them in production, with support at every step.

Engineers at Kaluza build with AI, and we mean that practically. From day one you’ll have paid access to Claude Code, with a budget we don’t ration, and we’ll teach you how we use it: planning work for agents, reviewing what they produce, and understanding every line that lands with your name on it. We care more about your judgement than your typing speed, and we’ll help you build both.

What you’ll do

• Build real product features from your first weeks : pick up well-shaped work in a product team, grow into shaping it yourself, and see it through to production.

• Work across the stack over time : depending on the team you’ll work across the interface people use, the services behind it, and the APIs between them, in whatever stack your team runs.

• Build with AI coding agents, and understand what they produce : break work down so an agent can take it, review the result as carefully as a colleague’s PR, and be able to explain every line you merge. We’ll teach you our way of working with them.

• Learn the systems you run : instrument what you ship, watch how it behaves in production, and shadow the on-call rota before you join it.

• Stay close to the people who use what you build : a supplier’s operations team, a customer plugging in a car at night. Ask why, and bring what you learn back to the team.

• Improve how the team works : tests, checks, docs and shared context that make the next person’s job easier, including the agents’.

What you’ll bring
These are the foundations and habits we see in engineers who do well here. Nobody arrives with all of them, and the junior end of this role exists so people can grow into them. If you’re excited by the role and can see yourself here, apply.

Ideally, you’ll have:

What will I be doing?

A technical leader in our Migration Enablement team, you will be responsible for the design, plan and build of the data migration for each of Kaluza’s platform deployments. The Migration Architect will be well-versed in the complexities and risks associated with data migration programmes, and be well-equipped to develop methodologies that reduce and remove these risks. 
You will be a key member of the Deployment Design team: a specialist unit focused on winning Kaluza new business and then delivering on the deals made. The team’s mission is to create seamless, scalable, and secure deployment solutions that empower our clients to accelerate innovation, achieve operational efficiency and business success. Through collaboration, a focus on repeatability, and a user-centred approach, we design and implement reliable SaaS deployment architectures that enhance performance, minimise risk, and support future growth.
Responsibilities will include -

• Source System & Data Architecture Analysis: Gaining a detailed understanding of clients’ existing systems, data models, integrations, business processes and data dependencies to determine migration requirements and complexity.

• Source-to-Target Data Mapping: Leading analysis and definition of mappings between legacy data structures and the Kaluza target data model, including transformation rules, defaults, derivations and handling of data gaps.

• Migration Solution Architecture: Designing end-to-end migration solutions covering data extraction, transformation, validation, loading, reconciliation and exception management, ensuring alignment with Kaluza architecture and engineering standards.

• Data Extraction Strategy: Consulting with and supporting clients in designing and developing robust extraction capabilities, including defining extract specifications, formats, sequencing, dependencies and data quality expectations.

• Migration Tooling & Engineering Collaboration: Working closely with Engineering teams to define requirements for migration tooling, APIs, ETL processes, validation frameworks and automation required to execute migrations safely and efficiently.

• API, Integration & ETL Expertise: Applying a strong understanding of APIs, integration patterns, ETL/ELT processes, data pipelines and large-scale data processing to design scalable migration approaches.

• Data Quality & Validation: Defining validation rules and data quality controls across extraction, transformation and loading, identifying data issues early and agreeing remediation approaches with clients and engineering teams.

• Migration Reconciliation: Designing reconciliation frameworks to demonstrate completeness and accuracy of migrated data, including source-to-target reconciliation, control totals, exception reporting and business validation.

• Client Solution Design: Architecting and presenting client-specific Kaluza migration solutions, clearly explaining technical design decisions, trade-offs, dependencies and the business outcomes the proposed approach will deliver.

• Migration Strategy & Planning: Developing client-specific migration strategies and plans, including migration cohorts, sequencing, volumes, frequency, throughput, eligibility criteria and migration windows.

• Migration Performance & Scalability: Assessing data volumes, processing capacity and system constraints to ensure migration solutions can achieve required throughput and scale while protecting platform stability.

• Migration Testing Strategy: Defining the technical migration testing approach across component testing, integration testing, end-to-end testing, migration dry runs, trial migrations and production readiness.

• Cutover & Production Migration Architecture: Designing the technical approach for migration cutover, including sequencing, dependencies, entry/exit criteria, rollback or recovery approaches, monitoring and operational readiness.

• Technical Migration Leadership: Acting as the technical authority for migration throughout implementation and live execution, providing technical direction, resolving complex issues and coordinating decisions across client, Engineering, Product and programme teams.

• Technical Governance & Design Assurance: Representing migration within programme and architecture governance, reviewing technical designs, managing architectural risks and dependencies, and ensuring migration solutions remain aligned with agreed standards.

• Issue & Root Cause Analysis: Leading investigation of complex migration failures and data issues, distinguishing between source-data, transformation, integration, platform and migration-tooling problems and driving appropriate resolution.

• Requirements & Technical Analysis: Translating business and migration requirements into clear technical requirements, specifications and acceptance criteria, while challenging assumptions and identifying gaps, dependencies and constraints.

• Migration Optimisation: Using evidence from testing, dry runs and live migrations to fine-tune migration rules, tooling, performance, sequencing and operational processes.

• Commercial & Pre-Sales Support: Leading the migration architecture elements of commercial proposals, including solution definition, technical feasibility, assumptions, dependencies, complexity assessment and estimation.

• Deployment & Implementation Architecture: Leading migration architecture within the broader client deployment and implementation design, ensuring migration is integrated effectively with platform configuration, integrations, testing and operational readiness.

• Technical Documentation & Migration Playbooks: Producing high-quality architecture documentation, technical specifications, data mapping artefacts and client-specific migration designs, while developing reusable Kaluza standards, patterns and playbooks to accelerate and standardise future migrations.

• Knowledge Sharing & Technical Enablement: Building migration capability across Kaluza by documenting lessons learned, establishing reusable architectural patterns and providing technical guidance and mentoring to engineering, implementation and migration teams.

About You 
You are a hands-on, analytical problem-solver who thrives at the intersection of technology and business. You have a passion for detail and a proven ability to translate complex client needs into practical, scalable solutions. You are comfortable working with large, diverse datasets and possess a strong understanding of how enterprise systems function.
Ideally, you'll have/be:

• Experience:  

• Experience within data migration programmes, with specific experience of developing Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) processes

• Experience in a technical/engineering leadership role, able to demonstrate leadership qualities

• Technical experience of Energy industry or utilities is a significant benefit

• Skills:

• Data analysis and management

• Systems architecture and software development

• Verbal and written communication including the ability to convey complex technical information to non-technical audiences

• Delivering impactful presentations as part of Kaluza sales activities

• Other Requirements: Kaluza is a global business, as a result the person in this role will be required to travel as part of commercial and deployment activities. By way of a guide, it’s expected that between 9 and 12 business trips a year will be required.

What will set you apart

• A passion for solving problems with multiple varied experiences of doing so;

• The determination to see a job done well from start to finish;

• A deep curiosit

• A track record in regulated markets where billing complexity matters, energy, telecoms, financial services, or similar. Familiarity with the French energy market (ENGIE, CRE, switching, tariff structures) is advantageous.

• Exceptional ability to translate abstract regulatory text or client requirements into clear, actionable, outcome-driven requirements for development teams.

• Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams (engineering, design, legal, operations, client success) to deliver localised solutions.

• Excellent stakeholder and client management skills , able to lead conversations across requirements, scope, expectations, and roadmap alignment, and communicate technical & market complexity clearly to varied audiences.

• Proficiency in AI tools throughout all stages of the product lifecycle — from discovery and ideation to delivery and iteration.Fluent in French and English — our platform and many of our teams operate in English, so you move easily between both.

• Fluent in French and very comfortable in English — our platform and many of our teams operate in English, so you move easily between both

Play to win, Solve the real problem, Build trust every day, Own the outcome, Go further together

Running a frontline business is an operational puzzle most software has never touched. Shift-by-shift labour costs, compliance that changes by region and by role, and margins thin enough that a badly built rota can sink a quarter. It's a harder problem than most white-collar SaaS, and yet frontline sectors employ 80% of the global workforce and have received about 1% of the last decade's software investment.
We think AI is what makes the problem solvable; better software alone wasn't enough. Frontline organisations sit on enormous amounts of operational data. Used properly, that data lets agents take on real parts of running the business rather than just reporting on it. That's what we're building at Sona, and it's early enough that the systems you build now will still be foundational in three years.
We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here .

You'll own a book of around 20-25 enterprise accounts across social care, hospitality and retail, partnering with Support, Product and Sales to own the post-live customer experience end to end. Some of the accounts you'll inherit are in difficult places, so you'll be rebuilding trust, holding rooms independently and driving outcomes in ambiguity.
We're a high-performance team. Everyone holds an important seat and is expected to perform at an elite level. We have each other's backs, we assume good intent, and we have zero space for internal politics. If that's your default, you'll thrive here.

arbeitnow:controls-engineer-london-unite.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.
 
🛠️ About our Robotics Team
The Robotics team is responsible for bridging the gap from our model to our vehicle platforms, in order to let the model focus on making driving decisions. We aim to provide high quality data to the model for making such decisions, whilst abstracting away platform-specific aspects. We combine specialisms across the robotics domain, blending strong theoretical foundations with solid engineering practice to span the spectrum from research to production.
 
🧠 Your day-to-day

• Develop, integrate, tune, and validate control, trajectory-generation, and action-processing algorithms across different vehicle platforms, operating modes, and challenging driving conditions, ensuring robust real-world performance

• Maintain and evolve our controls software architecture that connects AI Driver outputs to real-time vehicle actuation and feedback

• Own requirements, release readiness, and in-field performance and issue triage

• Implement and maintain production-quality, latency-sensitive control software in C++ for deployment to prototype, reference and production vehicles

• Use simulation, closed-loop evaluation and on-road testing to characterize controller behaviour, diagnose performance issues and validate improvements

• Work with teams across Wayve to define controller interfaces, integrate with adjacent systems and enable new vehicle platforms and product features (Ownership through the full lifecycle)

• Define and track quality metrics (e.g., comfort, tracking error, and safety margin KPIs, and regressions against them)

• Contribute to safety artefacts: provide evidence for safety cases, work with the safety team to ensure compliance with required standards

🧩 What you’ll be working on:
In this role you will develop and improve the vehicle trajectory and motion controllers that translate the Wayve AI Driver outputs into safe, smooth and robust vehicle motion across different vehicle platforms and applications (both ADAS and AV). You’ll tackle cutting-edge challenges: developing principled controls approaches, implementing real time systems, testing in complex scenarios and refining our evaluation pipelines. This is a great chance to make an impact on the AV industry and grow alongside a focused team of passionate experts at the forefront of autonomous driving technology.

🙌 You should apply if you have:
Required Skills/Experience

• Strong fundamentals in control theory, with applied experience in one or more of optimization, model-predictive control, numerical methods or dynamical systems

• Practical experience developing, tuning and validating motion control on complex real world physical systems (e.g., direct experience with mobile robotics and/or autonomous vehicles)

• Experience with test and validation discipline : unit and integration tests, simulation regression suites, closed-loop metrics.

• Strong software engineering skills, with experience building reliable production-quality systems in C++

• Experience with latency-sensitive or real-time software

• Ability to reason about and debug system-level behaviour in complex robotic systems across software and hardware

Desired Skills/Experience

• Applied machine learning experience, or experience developing systems that integrate with ML components

• Vehicle dynamics and actuation. Steering, braking and powertrain interfaces, actuator delay models, and CAN or similar vehicle bus experience

• Experience in the automotive industry, including ADAS or vehicle controls

• Experience with safety-critical systems, validation, and relevant industry standards (e.g. ISO 26262)

• Experience with monitoring and diagnostics: Logging, fault detection, and on-platform debugging tools, ideally with experience investigating field issues

• Experience across multiple platforms or vehicles. The team supports vehicle-to-vehicle variation, such as accounting for parameter identification, calibration, and keeping one software stack across hardware variants

 
🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.
 
More about Wayve:
🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.
Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.
 
How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:
Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.
 
🔍 The Interview Process:
Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

• Initial call / recruiter screen : general background, current situation, interests and Wayve company information & hiring context.

• Competency Interviews : programming and code review.

• Deep-dive technical interviews : domain knowledge & system design.

• Final interview : mission & values alignment.

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.
 
What’s in it for you (Location dependant):
💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more
 
A quick, honest note before you apply.
Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

About Artificial
Help shape the future of specialty insurance

At Artificial, we’re building the next generation of technology for the specialty (re)insurance market. Our mission is to transform how brokers and carriers operate in complex markets by removing operational barriers and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.
We use modern technology to solve real challenges for some of the world’s leading brokers and insurers. By automating the repetitive and structuring the complex, we help our partners unlock new opportunities for innovation and growth.
You’ll be joining a collaborative team that values curiosity, ownership, and continuous learning. We work in an environment where ideas are heard, support is built-in, and outcomes matter. Everyone here has the chance to make a tangible impact on our products, our customers, and the industry.
We've just raised $45M (£33M) in Series B funding from lead investor CommerzVentures, new investor Move Capital, as well as all existing shareholders. This investment round gives us the room to grow with confidence, continue to innovate, and ensure that Artificial remains the first choice for brokers and carriers seeking a smarter way to trade digitally.
Join us, and take the chance to be a part of something that will change the landscape of insurance for generations.
About the role
At Artificial, there are three primary sources of documentation we maintain:

• Client-facing product documentation for insurance business users (brokers, underwriters and operations teams using our platform)

• Our internal documentation site, which is our most heavily used documentation surface, built docs-as-code from the engineering repository and authored largely by engineers.

• Our public API documentation, owned and authored by our Integrations team from auto-generated OpenAPI specifications.

The below responsibilities break down how each of these three sources are to be managed.
Responsibilities

• Own the client-facing product documentation (1) end-to-end: strategy, information architecture, standards, tooling and content quality

• Own the internal documentation gap backlog (2):

• proactively identify potential gaps and triage incoming gap reports

• route each one to the best-placed author and chase it to completion

• write the content yourself where you're the right author

• Steward the internal documentation site (2) and public API documentation (3): set the standards, information architecture and editorial bar for content authored by engineering and integrations teams, and keep the publishing pipelines healthy

• Interview engineers about new features as they ship, and demystify them for non-technical readers before anyone has to ask

• Act as editorial reviewer on documentation changes, catching duplication, misplacement and unclear writing before it ships

• Write and maintain the highest-value client-facing content yourself: core product guides and release communications

• Select, build and run the documentation toolchain, including docs-as-code workflows (static site generators, CI/CD, review gates) where they serve us best

• Design and operate AI-assisted authoring pipelines that raise quality and throughput without sacrificing accuracy

• Build the contribution model: templates, style standards and review processes that let product managers and engineers contribute content you curate rather than gatekeep

• Partner with the Integrations team on API documentation: raise the quality of guides and examples around the auto-generated reference without taking authorship away from the experts

• Partner with product and customer-facing teams so documentation ships with releases, not after them

• Measure whether documentation is working: usage, search behaviour, support deflection and client feedback, and act on what you find

• Set the standard for clear technical communication across the company

About you

• 6+ years in technical writing, documentation engineering or a closely related discipline

• Preferably an ex Engineer who has stepped into technical writing / documentation

• Demonstrable experience producing end-user product documentation, plus enough developer documentation experience to edit and improve API guides credibly

• Hands-on experience owning documentation tooling, including docs-as-code workflows (for example Git-based authoring, static site generators, CI pipelines)

• A portfolio or writing samples that show you can make complex technical material clear for both technical and non-technical readers

• Used to working in a fast-paced, technological environment, with all the ambiguities this presents: flexibility will be needed

• Confident in reading and understanding code and pull requests, so that you are able to identify where documentation might need adding/editing

We especially want to hear from you if you have:

• Built or substantially restructured a documentation estate, not just contributed to one

• Experience establishing contribution models where engineers and product managers write and you edit and curate

• Practical experience using LLMs in documentation workflows, with a clear-eyed view of where they help and where they fail

• Familiarity with structured documentation frameworks such as Diataxis

• Familiarity with OpenAPI specifications and generating reference documentation from source

• Previously worked in a scale-up environment

• Come from an InsurTech, FinTech or other regulated-industry background

Benefits

• Private medical insurance

• Income protection insurance

• Life insurance of 4 * base salary

• On-site gym and shower facilities

• Enhanced maternity and paternity pay

• Team social events and company parties

• Salary exchange on pension and nursery fees

• Access to Maji, the financial wellbeing platform

• Company stock options managed through Ledgy

• Milestone Birthday Bonus and a Life Events leave policy

• Generous holiday allowance of 28 days plus national holidays

• Home office and equipment allowance, and a company MacBook

• Learning allowance and leave to attend conferences or take exams

• YuLife employee benefits, including EAP and bereavement helplines

• For each new hire, we plant a tree through our partnership with Ecologi Action

• The best coffee machine in London, handmade in Italy and imported just for us!
We’re proud to be an equal opportunities employer and are committed to building a team that reflects the diverse communities around us. If there’s anything you need to make the hiring process more accessible, just let us know—we’re happy to make adjustments. You’re also welcome to share your preferred pronouns with us at any point.
Think you don’t meet every requirement? Please apply anyway. We value potential as much as experience, and we know that raw talent counts.

About Artificial
Help shape the future of specialty insurance

About the role
Today, a key part of delivery has no clear owner: problem framing before configuration begins.

• On the customer side, there are rarely UX specialists - only domain experts and sponsors who describe needs as pre-formed solutions.

• On our side, configured workspaces are built by Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) in our Transform team: experts in the platform, accountable for shipping to a deadline, but not trained designers.

• Our Platform teams have design expertise but are often too far removed from individual implementations to influence the moments that matter most.

The result is pretty predictable: we move quickly into “how” before we are confident about the “what” and “why.”
Your mandate is to slow down at the right moment and make sure we’re solving the right problem - then help the team implement the best platform-valid solution.
This is a founding role. You would be the first Forward Deployed Designer (FDD) at Artificial, hired into an enabling function within the Platform team, with the mandate to define how the function works and to build it out. Later, FDDs would join the Transform teams in hands-on client roles: you’d take part in hiring them (with our support), then line-manage them directly.
Responsibilities
You would work closely with the Transform team and customers throughout discovery and delivery. In practice, that means:

• Establish the FDD function. Define the operating model, the patterns, and the ways of working from scratch.

• Grow and manage the team. Take part in hiring subsequent FDDs and line-manage them as they join.

• Join customer + FDE sessions early (problem framing and discovery), not only at reviews once decisions are already fixed.

• Translate requests into problems. For example, turn “we need a confirmation button before this step” into:

• the user behaviour driving the request

• two or three platform-valid approaches

• a recommendation, with trade-offs explained

• Prototype and test ideas quickly using the most effective medium (written specs, wireframes, workflows, or light code). We care more about clarity and platform realism than polished artefacts.

• Provide credible pushback when the customer’s proposed solution doesn’t address the underlying problem.

• Codify patterns and precedents so knowledge moves from individual memory into shared team infrastructure.

• Level up the FDE team’s design instincts over time. You shouldn’t be the only person who can think about UX across the two teams; part of the job is coaching, so the capability can spread.

• Use workspace signals (e.g. session data and call analysis) to surface risks early - before they become escalations.

About you
You are a designer who thrives in ambiguity and constraints, someone who can bring structure, judgement, and clarity to complex, real-world delivery.
You likely have experience in enterprise/B2B software where:

• the design system already exists

• the hard part is framing the right problem and navigating stakeholders

• solutions must work within meaningful technical and organisational constraints

You understand technical concepts fluently. Part of the role would involve writing code (with plenty of LLM and human assistance) using our in-house DSL (Domain Specific Language). We don’t want you to be an engineer, but we do need you to be comfortable reading and writing some code, reasoning about how a configurable system behaves, and understanding what the platform can and can’t express, well enough to hold a credible conversation with engineers and to explain these constraints to customers when necessary.
You have managed designers. You’re comfortable with line management of a small team (roughly three to five people) and have hired designers before. Early on, you’d do this hands-on yourself; as the function grows, you’d manage the FDDs who follow.
Insurance or Lloyd’s experience is a plus, but is not a requirement. We care more about how you think about complex platforms and stakeholders than about prior domain knowledge, which you can learn here.
We especially want to hear from you if you have

• Collaborative skills with an emphasis on product quality.

• Experience in insurtech, insurance or related industries.

• Strong problem-solving skills.

• Experience in a distributed work environment.
