arbeitnow:founding-product-manager-germa.title: Founding Product Manager (German-speaking)
arbeitnow:founding-product-manager-germa.description:
About BoWatt
BoWatt is building agentic requirements and systems engineering software for manufacturing.

We believe AI will reach PhD-level engineering capability within the next 10 years. This will unlock massive value across complex manufacturing industries. Cars. Planes. Rockets. Factories. Chips. Medical devices. All will be engineered with agents.

We bootstrapped BoWatt to €500k+ ARR before raising our first round. BoWatt is backed by tier-1 investors, including Atlantic Foodlabs, Buildery (CDTM affiliates), and Prequel Ventures, along with angels from Cohere and Luminovo.

You’ll join a small team of startup builders focused on speed, ownership, and execution. Over half the team are former founders, with backgrounds across DeepTech AI, gaming, and other startups. We’ve studied and worked at institutions and companies including Stanford, TUM, Google, EA, and YC-backed AI startups.

The role
As our Founding Product Manager, you will help determine what BoWatt builds, why we build it, and whether it creates meaningful value for customers.

You will work closely across our commercial, customer success and engineering teams, as well as with our customers. You will develop a deep understanding of complex engineering workflows, turn customer problems into clear product opportunities, and drive initiatives from discovery through launch and iteration.

This is a hands-on product role. You will spend time with customers, work through technical and operational detail, write requirements, make trade-offs, test solutions, and help the team ship quickly.

• Lead product discovery - translate complex workflows and customer needs into clear product requirements and success criteria

• Develop a deep understanding of how manufacturing and systems-engineering teams work

• Identify and define the highest-value customer problems for BoWatt to solve

• Help own and prioritise the product roadmap

• Balance strategic opportunities, recurring customer needs, commercial importance, and engineering effort

• Drive product initiatives from initial discovery through scoping, development, launch, and iteration

• Give engineers the context and clarity needed to make strong implementation decisions

• Prototype and test potential solutions with customers before and during development

• Work with Customer Success to turn individual customer feedback into scalable product improvements

• Use qualitative feedback and product data to understand adoption and evaluate whether features are working

• Triage product issues and bugs, make clear prioritisation decisions, and coordinate with Engineering

• Improve BoWatt’s processes for discovery, prioritisation, product delivery, launches, and feedback

• Develop deep expertise in BoWatt’s product, customers, and target industries

During your first six months, you will work closely with our engineering team to build the domain and product knowledge required to take ownership of increasingly important product areas.

You

• You are deeply curious about customers and want to understand how their work actually happens

• You enjoy turning complex, ambiguous problems into clear product decisions

• You combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution

• You can distinguish between an individual customer request and a scalable product opportunity

• You make thoughtful trade-offs and are comfortable deciding with incomplete information

• You write clearly, communicate confidently, and know how to get to the point

• You are comfortable working closely with software engineers and discussing technical constraints

• You move quickly without losing sight of product quality or customer outcomes

• You take ownership of results rather than simply managing tickets and meetings

• You want to build a product function rather than inherit an established playbook

• You are ambitious, resourceful, and excited to become an expert in a complex industry

Requirements

• At least two years of experience in Product Management, Product Ownership, Product Operations, or a comparable product-building role

• Experience shipping B2B software in close collaboration with engineers

• Experience conducting product discovery and translating customer problems into clear requirements

• Strong prioritisation, project management, and stakeholder-management skills

• The ability to understand technical products and communicate with engineers, technical users, and business stakeholders

• Fluent German required; English is our internal working language

• Four days per week in our Munich office at Balanstraße

• Experience with enterprise software, AI products, manufacturing, engineering, systems engineering, or early-stage startups is a bonus

What we offer

• Competitive salary based on experience

• Participation in BoWatt’s Founders Pool: 5–10% virtual equity package

• Significant ownership over an important part of BoWatt’s product

• The opportunity to help build BoWatt’s product function and ways of working

• 25 vacation days per year, plus public holidays

• Company retreats

• WellPass membership

The Founders Pool
BoWatt’s Founders Pool is a dedicated virtual-equity pool for a small group of early team members who take responsibility for building and leading a major part of the company.
 
We created it because we want the people building BoWatt alongside us to participate meaningfully in the value they help create. These are not narrow execution roles with finished playbooks. You will own your vertical with co-founder-like autonomy and accountability: setting the standard, making difficult trade-offs, and being responsible for the results.
 
As our Founding Product Manager, you will participate in the Founders Pool (5-10%) and take meaningful ownership of how BoWatt’s product develops. The precise allocation, vesting structure, and plan terms will be discussed transparently during the interview process.

Interview process

• 20-minute screening call

• 90-minute live product case (CEO and team member)

• 60-minute culture interview (CEO)

• Reference checks & Offer

We aim to complete the entire interview process within 14 days.

Drive Business Development Operations (30%)

We are looking forward to your application!

Sunday Natural emerged from a long-standing passion and research in the fields of health, healing, and personal growth. The lack of natural, high-quality products on the market was the original motivation for founding Sunday Natural in 2013. We aim to produce the products we ourselves would love to buy – as natural as possible, absolutely pure, free from any additives, and of the highest quality. In a strategic partnership with CVC, Sunday Natural is now one of Germany's most renowned quality manufacturers, with its own research and development department in Berlin. For the continuous improvement of our products, we collaborate with selected research institutes, scientists, therapists, farmers, and professional associations.

Our diverse team in Berlin consists of over 400 employees from more than 45 nationalities and continues to grow – but at a sustainable pace. Our goal is to foster a collaborative, supportive, and inclusive work environment with a diverse group of motivated, talented, and visionary team members.

We highly value equality of opportunity and inclusivity, and we would like to particularly encourage women and candidates from under-represented backgrounds to apply, even if you don’t match with 100% of the requirements.

arbeitnow:deployment-strategist-london-2.title: Deployment Strategist
arbeitnow:deployment-strategist-london-2.description:
Who We Are
Serval is an AI-native automation platform transforming how enterprises operate. We build intelligent agents that understand real-world workflows and execute them end-to-end — replacing manual processes and rigid legacy systems with adaptive, learning software. Founded in early 2024, Serval is already trusted by companies like Fox, Notion, Perplexity, Vercel, and Brex to automate high-volume, high-friction operational work across their organizations.

At the core of Serval is an agentic AI platform that turns natural language into production-grade workflows. Our agents don’t just respond to requests — they reason, take action across systems, and continuously improve with usage. What began with operational use cases has quickly evolved into a horizontal AI automation layer used across IT, HR, Finance, Security, Legal, and Engineering.

Our mission is to eliminate repetitive, manual work across the enterprise and give teams leverage through intelligent automation. Long term, we’re building the universal AI operations layer — a system of agents that sits across business functions and runs the workflows that keep modern companies moving.

We’re backed by leading investors including Sequoia Capital, Redpoint Ventures, Meritech, First Round, General Catalyst, Elad Gil, and others.

About the team
The Agent Deployment team is a customer-facing technical team, central to how Serval turns product capability into real business outcomes. The org is a family of roles: Deployment Strategists are the primary technical relationship and AI advisor for each customer, partnering with Deployed Software Engineers to build enterprise-grade features and products. Deployment Success Managers own each customer's long-term success, building the systems and motions that scale adoption, expansion, and renewal well past go-live.

Role Overview
As a Deployment Strategist on Serval's Agent Deployment team, you’ll be the primary technical relationship for Serval’s customers: guiding their deployments, advising their AI strategy, and owning their outcomes. You’ll work deeply within Serval’s existing product surface area: building novel workflows, configuring integrations, and shipping bug fixes and product changes yourself.
This role is for someone who thrives on execution velocity, moving quickly across multiple engagements at once. You’re at home in ambiguity and bring a strong blend of technical depth, product sense, and customer obsession. And because you sit closest to how customers actually use Serval, you'll directly shape our product roadmap: the workflows and features you build in the field make their way into the core product.

What You’ll Do

• Own customer engagements from pilot through production launch: design and deliver deployments that fit each customer's workflows and scale adoption of Serval.

• Build AI agents: design and build AI agents on Serval's platform that drive real value for customers.

• Advise AI strategy: embed with customers to guide and shape how they adopt and scale AI.

• Lead migrations: design and execute migration plans that minimize disruption and ensure seamless adoption of Serval's platform.

• Partner cross-functionally: work with Engineering, Sales, and Marketing to turn field learnings into repeatable processes and a sharper go-to-market.

What You’ll Need

• Degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience.

• 5+ years in a relevant role (product, engineering, consulting, founder).

• Strong communication and relationship management skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Hands-on technical ability: reading and troubleshooting production code in customer-facing environments, analyzing code paths, database state, and API requests/responses with infra and browser dev tools.

• Working knowledge of APIs and REST, IAM, and SQL for data analysis.
 

Nice to Have

• Experience in an early-stage startup environment.

• Experience writing production code.

• Background working with enterprise customers or complex technical sales cycles.

• Familiarity with IT, security, service management, or workflow automation.

What We Offer

• Impact : Be a key player in shaping the success of our product and company.

• Growth : Build a fundamentally new AI product offering with the support of our experienced team and investors. Grow rapidly with the company.

• Culture : Join a culture that values innovation, ownership, accountability, and fun.

Compensation: £115K – £210K • Offers Equity

arbeitnow:sales-director-london-121162.description:
About 9fin
9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.
Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.
Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.
We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.

About the Role
We’re looking for a Sales Director to lead the volume end of our Sales organization in EMEA. Tiers 2 and 3 make up the broad base of our client portfolio: a large number of banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms and advisors, with smaller account sizes than our Tier 1 and strategic clients. Retention, expansion and coverage at scale drive growth here.
You’ll lead a team of 6–8 Account Managers, each owning a book of Tier 2 and Tier 3 clients, and a small number of Account Executives winning new clients in the same tiers. You’ll own renewals and net retention for the segment, build a repeatable operating rhythm across a high volume of accounts, and grow a team within our newly tiered sales organization.
This is a hands-on leadership role reporting to the Head of Sales, EMEA & APAC. You’ll combine coaching with disciplined pipeline and forecast management, and you’ll be accountable for how your team performs against its number.
What you’ll work on
Every day is different, but here’s an example of the kind of things you’ll work on:

• Lead the Tier 2 and Tier 3 EMEA team to consistent, forecastable delivery quarter over quarter.

• Own segment net retention and expansion, and make sure every account has a renewal plan well ahead of its date.

• Coach and manage a team of 6–8 Account Managers, and Account Executive, through weekly pipeline, renewal and forecast reviews.

• Set coverage models and account prioritization so your team spends its time where the revenue and risk are.

• Run a clear operating cadence across the segment, including book and territory planning, account plans and a shared methodology.

• Recruit, onboard and develop the team, including training on demos, usage analysis and client reviews.

• Manage performance through structured reviews, goal setting and development plans.

• Partner with Customer Success, Sales Engineering, Enablement, Rev Ops, Marketing and Product to remove barriers to growth and bring client feedback into the roadmap.

• Work with the Head of Sales, EMEA & APAC and the US team to keep handovers, tiering and territories consistent globally.

• Keep accurate CRM records and forecasts, and use the data to coach and make decisions.

About You
This role will be a great fit if you:

• Have 5+ years of experience leading account management or commercial teams, ideally in capital markets, fintech or data and SaaS.

• Have a track record of managing high-volume books and delivering retention and growth across them.

• Are comfortable owning a team number and can show how you’ve consistently hit it.

• Are a proactive coach, not a reactive manager. You share process, help your team plan ahead and don’t wait for forecasts to slip.

• Have run a disciplined cadence of pipeline reviews, forecasting and account planning.

• Have a good knowledge of financial markets and the ability to build relationships across the buy side, sell side and advisory community.

• Are comfortable with CRM tools (Salesforce preferred) and use data to drive decisions.

• Build trust across a matrixed commercial organization and partner effectively with Customer Success, Sales Engineering, Enablement, Rev Ops and Product.

• Thrive in ambitious, fast-moving environments where expectations are high, opportunities are abundant, and no two days look the same.

Our benefits
We’re a scaling start up, and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.
 
Financial & Insurance

• Competitive Salary (our salary bands are benchmarked at the top end of the market)

• Equity options

• Pension (your minimum contributions are 4% with 9fin matching up to 7%)

• Private Medical Insurance

• Paid sick leave with Income Protection for long periods of illness

• Group Life Assurance

• Season Ticket Loan & Cycle to Work schemes

Time off

• 25 holiday days per year

• Local public holidays (with the ability to exchange them for alternative days)

• Work abroad for up to 3 months a year

• 1 month paid sabbatical after 5 years of service

• Enhanced parental leave & flexible working arrangements available

Growth & Culture

• Professional learning and development budget

• Bi-annual team socials

• Summer and Winter company social events

 

Hybrid Policy
9fin is a hybrid company, and the office is a regular part of how we work. From January 2027, all employees will work from their designated 9fin office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Some teams may be asked to be in the office more often, where the nature of their work calls for it. For the rest of the week, you may work from wherever works best for you and your team. Your Talent Partner will share hybrid working details for this role.

9fin is an equal opportunities employer
At 9fin we are dedicated to building and promoting a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone can reach their full potential and truly belong. We recognize that building diverse teams enables a more creative and productive environment. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might just be who we’re looking for — either for this role, or perhaps another.

Maya HTT is a world leading developer of digital industries software solutions. The world’s top tier engineering and manufacturing organizations rely on Maya’s experience and expertise to achieve the full potential of their software investment. Maya HTT is also a Value Added Reseller (VAR) for the Siemens PLM Software products, with a focus on CAE-based simulation and providing engineering services, including software training, migration, implementation, and custom development, along with consulting.

Position Summary
We’re looking for an experienced Senior NX CAD Application Engineer to join our UK team. In this role, you’ll be a trusted technical partner to our customers, helping leading engineering organizations solve complex design challenges and get more value from Siemens NX and the broader digital engineering ecosystem. You’ll bring deep NX CAD expertise while taking a broader view of customer success - helping lead technical projects, supporting other engineers, identifying opportunities for automation and innovation, AI adoption and making sure solutions deliver real value for our customers. This is an ideal opportunity for an experienced NX professional who wants to move beyond traditional CAD support into a role with greater technical ownership, customer responsibility, and deliver digital engineering transformation via automations and AI.
 
What You’ll Do

• Serve as a senior subject matter expert for Siemens NX CAD and NX best practices.

• Explore and leverage AI to provide agentic solutions to improve engineering workflows and customer outcomes.

• Build trusted relationships with customers, understanding their engineering challenges and proactively helping them identify solutions.

• Deliver high-quality NX CAD consulting services and technical training.

• Mentor and support other engineers working on NX-related projects.

What You Bring

• 10+ years of industrial experience working with Siemens NX CAD, (product design, configuring and administering NX environments)

• UK nationality (British citizenship) is required due to the nature of the projects associated with this role.

• An interest in applying AI and emerging technologies to engineering and product development workflows.

Nice to Have

• Experience with NX Open, NX journaling, or NX automation/customisation.

• Experience with scripting or programming, such as Python, TCL, C#, C++, or similar technologies.

• Exposure to Teamcenter or other PLM systems, particularly from an NX user or power-user perspective.

• Experience with NX CAM, NX Post Builder, Siemens Post Configurator, or related manufacturing tools.

• Experience with Solid Edge or other commercial CAD platforms.

• Experience delivering or supporting design automation solutions.

• Experience mentoring engineers or informally leading technical teams.

• Experience with additive manufacturing or other advanced manufacturing technologies.

You’ll become one of the senior technical anchors for NX within our UK team - someone customers and colleagues can rely on when a problem is complex, when a project needs technical leadership, or when an opportunity requires connecting CAD expertise with automation, PLM, software, or emerging technologies.

arbeitnow:graduate-mechanical-design-eng.description:
Company
NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.
Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.
Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.
Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.
Hiring now
We are hiring as soon as possible. This role is for someone who has already graduated, or who will complete their degree in time to start with us very soon. We are not able to consider final-year students who graduate in summer 2027 or later, and this is not a graduate scheme with a fixed annual intake.

Role Overview
This is a first full-time engineering role on the NEO-1 satellite. You will design satellite hardware and help keep the satellite's full CAD assembly organised as the design matures, learning from our lead designer and working in a small, multidisciplinary team. You will take ownership of real parts early, translate requirements into manufacturable designs and support their validation through prototyping and environmental testing.

Key Responsibilities

• Design and develop mechanical hardware for the satellite, such as brackets, panels, component mounts, thermal-control hardware and cable and harness routing, with guidance from the lead designer.

• Work in the satellite's large 3D CAD assembly alongside the wider design team, learning how to keep interfaces, configurations and revisions in step as several designers work in the same model.

• Support assembly configuration, PLM data (3DEXPERIENCE ('3DX') or similar), bills of materials and engineering change control (ECO/ECR/ECN), so that models, drawings and interfaces stay consistent as changes are released.

• Run interference and clash checks and help maintain the digital mock-up, working with each subsystem owner to allocate space and resolve conflicts.

• Produce dimensioned, manufacturing-ready drawings using GD&T, with review from senior engineers.

• Support design reviews (PDR and CDR) and qualification, working with structural and thermal engineers.

• Work with manufacturers and suppliers to make designs easier to build, and to balance cost, mass and reliability.

• Support prototype builds, integration and environmental test campaigns, iterating designs based on results.

• Collaborate with electrical, software, systems and thermal engineers to integrate mechanical components into the satellite platform.

Required Skills & Experience

• Bachelor's or master's degree in mechanical, aerospace or a related engineering discipline, completed or completing very soon.

• Hands-on 3D CAD skills from university projects, a placement or an internship (SolidWorks preferred; CATIA, NX or Creo also considered).

• Working knowledge of GD&T and experience producing engineering drawings, including from coursework or a team project.

• Solid grounding in mechanical design principles, materials and thermal management, with a working understanding of structural mechanics.

• Evidence of designing, building and testing something real, such as a placement project, Formula Student, a UAV, or a rocketry or satellite team, including troubleshooting and iteration.

• Clear communicator who is comfortable explaining and defending design decisions, and open to feedback and challenge in a fast-moving team.

Preferred Experience

• A placement, internship or year in industry in aerospace, space, motorsport or another high-reliability field.

• Experience of several people working in one CAD assembly, for example in a Formula Student or university team, including how files and revisions were controlled.

• Exposure to PLM or PDM systems (for example 3DEXPERIENCE ('3DX'), Windchill, Teamcenter, ENOVIA or SolidWorks PDM) or to formal engineering change processes (ECO/ECR/ECN).

• Experience of design reviews, documented requirements and standards.

• Satellite, CubeSat or rocketry project experience, including hardware that has launched.

• Basic FEA familiarity and exposure to manufacturing processes.

Why NewOrbit Space?

• Pioneering space technology - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.

• Ownership and impact - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.

• Equity and competitive salary - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.

• Comprehensive benefits - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups.

• Hybrid working - One dedicated remote day per week.

• Visa sponsorship and relocation support - We sponsor visas and provide relocation support for candidates moving to join us.

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.
We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

• ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

• ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

• ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

• High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

• Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

• AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

• Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

• Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

• Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

• Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

• Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

• Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

• Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

• Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role
We build an ads engine that learns as it goes: brand book, taste, and what actually performs in every market. It plans, generates, localizes, launches and learns from ads across the major ad platforms, using ElevenLabs’ full audio and video stack.
You’ll be a founding engineer for a product area of your own. There’s no PM and no handed-down spec. You’ll talk to users, decide what to build, and ship it across the stack, from data pipelines and agent tools to the UI. Early work could include feeding competitive intelligence into the engine’s weekly briefs or launching a new ad format.
We’re looking for founders and founding engineers. You’d rather ship a rough v0 on Friday than a perfect design doc. Strong engineering is the minimum. What sets people apart is product judgment and ownership.

Requirements

• Has built and shipped a product end-to-end without anyone handing them a spec, ideally as a founder or one of the first engineers.

• Strong full-stack product engineer (frontend- or backend-leaning is fine) who can build a pipeline, an agent tool and the UI

• Builds with LLMs and agents pragmatically: tools, retrieval and evals, not model research.

• Talks to users without being asked, and can say what they’d build first and why.

Bonus: experience with ad platforms, adtech or marketing tools; analytics and attribution; web builders and CMSs; taste in creative.

Location
This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere between the US East Coast and India, with the ability to operate in European timezones required. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in Bangalore, Dublin, London, New York and Warsaw.

You will drive multi-quarter platform initiatives that improve delivery velocity, system reliability, and product quality through systems validation. Working closely with Product Management and partner engineering teams, you will turn complex, ambiguous challenges into clear execution plans and raise the bar for engineering quality and operational excellence.

About Nscale

At Nscale, we are building the infrastructure for Europe’s AI revolution. Nscale is developing cutting-edge, sovereign generative AI solutions powered by a new generation of high-performance, sustainable data centers and GPUs built specifically for AI workloads.

The rapid growth of artificial intelligence is driving unprecedented global demand for compute and GPU infrastructure. Positioned at the heart of this transformation, Nscale is delivering the platforms that will enable the next decade of innovation.

Working closely with the world’s most advanced AI technology providers, Nscale integrates next-gen compute hardware and GPU clusters across both partner and self-delivered facilities. This is a unique opportunity to join Nscale’s journey, play a pivotal role in delivering transformative AI infrastructure, and help shape a company designed to scale rapidly across Europe and beyond.

The Role

We’re looking for an experienced Commercial Manager with a strong Quantity Surveying / Construction Cost Management background to manage commercial and contractual aspects of Nscale’s Hyperscale Data Centre projects in the UK & Europe.

Reporting to the Commercial Director, you will be responsible for the commercial management of projects — overseeing procurement, cost control, forecasting, contract administration, and financial reporting from pre-contract through to final account.

This role requires a commercially astute professional with excellent attention to detail and a hands-on approach to project delivery. You will work collaboratively with Development, Design, and Construction teams to ensure that each project is delivered on budget, on time, and in full compliance with contractual and governance requirements.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the commercial management of major hyperscale data centre construction projects, ensuring delivery within approved budgets, timelines, and Nscale standards.
  • Drive cost efficiency and value creation, optimising expenditure while maintaining financial discipline, commercial control, and alignment with business and project objectives.
  • Own and manage detailed project budgets and CAPEX models, providing accurate financial data and scenario analysis to support decision-making.
  • Prepare and deliver detailed cost reports, forecasts, and cash flow analyses, ensuring accuracy, transparency, and timely insight into project financial performance.
  • Conduct budget preparation and benchmarking exercises, including detailed cost modelling and comparative analysis, and review outcomes with senior management.
  • Analyse and present cost reports to senior management, providing commentary, trend analysis, and recommendations to inform executive decision-making.
  • Manage project costs throughout the lifecycle, including cost validation, variations analysis, value engineering, and cost-saving initiatives to enhance overall project value.
  • Oversee financial close-out processes, including reconciliation of budgets, settlement of vendor accounts, and completion of all final commercial documentation.
  • Manage and provide guidance on commercial change management, including change evaluation, negotiation, and approval in line with contractual and governance requirements.
  • Lead commercial risk management activities, identifying and mitigating risks proactively, maintaining live risk registers, and implementing strategies to minimise exposure.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Development, Construction, Finance, and Operations teams, ensuring that commercial objectives are aligned with design, schedule, and operational goals.
  • Stay informed on regional market trends, cost indices, and regulatory developments, applying insights to continuously refine Nscale’s commercial approach and maintain best-in-class delivery standards.

Who You Are

  • 7+ years’ experience in forecasting, cash flow management, cost control, and profitability across complex Construction projects / portfolios, with experience within Data Centres
  • Degree-qualified in Quantity Surveying, Commercial Management, or a related discipline; MRICS or equivalent professional accreditation advantageous.
  • Proven track record of delivering profitable projects and optimizing commercial performance
  • Able to engage effectively across regions, time zones, and disciplines.
  • Adaptable, proactive, and energised by working in a high-growth, fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.
  • Fluency in English required; other European languages a plus.

Why Join Nscale?

  • Be part of a fast-moving, high-growth Necoloud company driving and delivering sustainable, next-generation AI infrastructure.
  • High-performing scale-up culture built on autonomy, accountability, and execution excellence.
  • 25 days holiday + bank holidays (33 days total)
  • Highly competitive compensation including ESOP (equity options)
  • Progression opportunities – we grow, you grow.
  • Hybrid / remote working options with ~ 25% travel to project sites across UK & Europe

arbeitnow:director-emea-professional-ser.description:
About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.
With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.
Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

About the Role
We are looking for a Director, EMEA Professional Services to build and lead our services and customer engineering motion across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.
This is a player-coach leadership role at the center of the EMEA go-to-market. You will shape how we engage EMEA customers after the sale and alongside it. You will help Sales position and sell both the subscription and, when it fits, services. You will own staffing and delivery for EMEA engagements. You will also coordinate the wider Customer Engineering team in region, including Enablement Engineers, Activation Specialists, and Account Managers.
You will work closely with EMEA GTM leadership and stay aligned with global Professional Services leadership. EMEA should feel like one team with the rest of PS, with the local context it needs to win.
Location: London preferred. Open to other EMEA locations with strong overlap with UK and European business hours. Some travel to customers and to our San Francisco and New York offices is expected.
What You'll Do

• Define EMEA Customer Engineering programs: Partner with EMEA GTM leadership to design and run programs for the region. This includes onboarding, activation, enablement, and services offerings. Adapt global programs to regional needs such as data residency, regulated industries, language, and partner ecosystems.

• Support positioning and selling: Support the creation and evolution of standard pre sales assets to support the AEs with positioning Professional Services. Work with Account Executives and Solutions Engineers on deal strategy. Help position the subscription and the right post-sale path for each customer. Join executive conversations when needed. Scope and sell Professional Services when it is the right fit. Review SOWs, estimates, and pricing for EMEA deals.

• Own resource management and delivery: Own staffing, capacity planning, and utilization for the EMEA PS team. Match engagements to the right people and practices. Make sure delivery follows PS methodology, including scoping, technical review, documentation, and customer handoff. Review key deliverables, surface risk early, and handle escalations.

• Lead and grow the EMEA team: Hire, onboard, coach, and develop Architects, AI Engineers, and Engagement Managers in region. Set clear expectations and give direct feedback. Build a team culture with a high bar for quality and craft.

• Coordinate across global Customer Engineering in a matrix model: Provide day-to-day coordination and supervision for EMEA Enablement Engineers, Activation Specialists, and Account Managers. Set shared priorities and make sure customers get a connected journey from activation to enablement to services to expansion. Work with their functional leaders on performance, growth, and standards.

• Align with global PS leadership: Keep delivery standards, tooling, pricing, and reporting consistent across regions. Share what works in EMEA. Bring back playbooks, reusable assets, and process improvements from the global team. Contribute to the PS operating rhythm and roadmap.

• Run the business: Own EMEA PS bookings, utilization, delivery margin, and customer outcomes. Report on pipeline, capacity, and risk to Customer Engineering and GTM leadership.

• Stay close to customers: Remain active in key accounts. Act as the senior escalation point for strategic EMEA customers. Be a credible voice with technical and executive stakeholders.

What You'll Bring

• You have 10+ years of experience in professional services, solutions engineering, customer engineering, or consulting. At least 4 of those years were in leadership roles.

• You have led a services or post-sales team in EMEA. You know the regional market and its regulatory landscape.

• You have helped sell technical services alongside a software subscription. You can scope work, price it, and defend it with customers.

• You have owned resource management and delivery. You understand utilization, capacity planning, and delivery quality.

• You have led through influence in a matrix organization. You can set direction for people who do not report to you.

• You are credible with engineers and executives. You can discuss agent architectures, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise AI adoption.

• You have built programs from scratch in a fast-moving environment. You do not wait to be told what to do.

• You communicate clearly and directly. You work well across time zones with a global team.

You exemplify our operating principles

• You are motivated to build something great. You hold a high bar for quality, craft, and impact.

• You embrace hot takes. You share informed opinions, challenge the status quo, and engage in constructive debate.

• You operate with maximum agency. You take ownership, move work forward independently, and help others unblock.

• You run to the roar. You lean into hard problems, ambiguity, and fast-moving challenges.

Nice to Have

• Hands-on experience with AI/ML, LLM applications, or agent frameworks

• Experience with SaaS subscriptions, usage-based pricing, and services attach

• Experience working with SIs and cloud marketplaces in EMEA

• Experience in a high-growth startup or open-source company

• Fluency in one or more European languages in addition to English

How Success Will Be Measured

• EMEA customers have clear programs and a connected post-sale journey.

• Services attach rate and bookings grow in the region, with healthy margins.

• EMEA PS meets its utilization target over time, with exceptions understood and managed.

• Delivery consistently follows PS standards, and material risks surface early.

• Matrix partners in Enablement, Activation, and Account Management are aligned on EMEA priorities.

• EMEA practices stay consistent with global PS and feed improvements back to it.

Compensation and Benefits
We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. Actual compensation and offerings will vary based on role, level, and location. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

arbeitnow:staff-product-engineer-london-.description:
Hi 👋 I’m Rich Ashworth, Director of Engineering at hyperexponential.
I lead the Model Authoring value stream that owns the products our customers use to write and manage their pricing models. An actuary might start with an Excel rater and finish with a Python model that has been reviewed, approved, and is pricing live business. Our job is to turn that into an exceptional user experience and make every step of that credible enough to trust.
I'm hiring a Staff Product Engineer to help set our technical direction and build the next version of our products. It's an individual contributor role, but influence is a huge part of it: the standards the pods work to, the shared enablers underneath the product, and the interfaces where our problems meet other teams'. You’ll be hands-on where the risk is highest.
There's no established playbook for any of this, but there’s an incredible opportunity in front of us. If this sounds like a role that would excite you, I'd love to hear from you.

About hyperexponential (hx)
At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.
Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.
Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.
What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.
What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.
If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the Model Authoring team
Model Authoring owns the products our customers use to write and manage their pricing models: the model developer experience and our actuarial agent. An actuary might start with an Excel-based rater and finish with a Python model that has been reviewed, approved and is pricing live business. Our job is to make every step of that credible enough to trust. The team is distributed across our Warsaw and London offices.
As the Staff Product Engineer, you will help set the team's technical direction. This is an individual contributor role, but influence is a large part of it: you'll help define the standards the team works to, raise the technical bar across pods, and own the interfaces where our problems meet those of teams elsewhere in Technology. You'll be expected to move fast and start shaping technical conversations early. We work in an AI-native way, and you'll help define and evolve what that means here.

What you'll be doing

• Establish a set of engineering standards across the Model Authoring pods. The standards are documented and actively referenced in code review, with new pod work conforming by default.

• Set and own the technical direction for the team's shared enablers, including how we represent and persist models, the model registry, secure context access, and shared agentic infrastructure.

• Establish the technical interfaces between Model Authoring and other parts of the business. Dependencies with other teams are agreed, documented, and progressing without needing to be brokered by someone else.

• Work hands-on on the hardest problems in the stream. This is not an advisory role: we would expect you in the code where the risk is highest.

• Help define how we work in an AI-native way. Which parts of model development and of our own engineering we hand to agents, what stays human, and what evidence we need before trusting either.

• Visibly lift the engineers around you. You're sought out for design input across pods, and there's at least one engineer whose growth is clearly attributable to your support.

What you'll need to have done

• Worked in an AI-native environment, and genuinely want to keep doing so. You've used AI or agentic tools in your own engineering workflow, introduced or experimented with them, and have a real view on what's worked and what hasn't.

• Been product-focused rather than purely technical. You understand who your users are, where their pain points are, and how your technical decisions connect to commercial outcomes.

• Set technical direction while navigating genuine ambiguity. A proven track record of owning architecture in a domain with no established playbook, and making clear calls on imperfect information rather than deferring them.

• Owned a significant technical challenge or service end to end, with the depth to walk through it in detail - the trade-offs, the contracts, the things you'd do differently.

• Influenced across teams. You can hold a position under challenge, genuinely listen to pushback, and persuade others - not just present your own view and hope it lands.

• Worked effectively across distributed teams - this role spans our Warsaw and London offices, so you'll need to be comfortable building relationships and influence across both.

You're unlikely to thrive here if

• You'd rather focus purely on the technical problem than get close to users, customer pain points, and the commercial implications of what you build.

• You're not comfortable setting technical direction in ambiguity, or you'd rather wait for an established playbook than make a call on imperfect information.

• You're not excited about helping define what the future of software engineering looks like and are prepared to embrace tooling and new ways of working to support this.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Compensation
At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.
Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits
£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.
25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).
Company pension scheme via Penfold.
Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life .
Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.
Private healthcare insurance through AXA.
Income protection and Life Insurance.
Cycle to Work Scheme.

Additional perks
Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).
Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.
Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.
Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

Interview process

• Initial call with our Talent team

• Hiring Manager Interview

• Skills Assessment & follow-up interview

• Values Interview

• Meet the CEO

Our commitment to Diversity
hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.
Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.
If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

A little about us
incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Notion, Linear, Ramp and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.
The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.
We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

The role in one line
Being a GRC Engineer at incident.io means turning compliance from spreadsheets and screenshots into something that just runs, so “can you prove it?” gets answered before anyone asks.
What that looks like day to day
As a GRC Engineer at incident.io , you own how we prove we’re doing the right thing: our compliance programme, our customer security questionnaires, and the evidence behind both. One day you’re building an AI workflow that drafts questionnaire answers, the next you’re pushing our ISO 27001 work forward, the next you’re telling the product team what makes GRC painful.
Our GRC programme is young, and Slack is our system of record. You’ll make it scale, using AI-powered tooling and workflows to take the toil out of audits, evidence collection and customer questions.
Right now, that means:

• ISO 27001. It’s in progress, and you’ll help raise the bar and get us over the line.

• ISO 42001. We build AI products, so we want to manage AI responsibly. In your first two quarters or so, you’ll run a gap assessment against the standard.

• Dogfooding. We use incident.io for our own security work, and you’ll drive product improvements that make GRC less painful for our customers too.

You’ll work closely with the wider security team, engineering, legal and product.
Who you are

• You’ve run or contributed to a real compliance programme, ideally ISO 27001, and you know what it takes to get through an audit.

• You’d rather automate evidence collection than chase people for screenshots.

• You write code (Python, Go or similar) or build workflows, and you’re excited about using AI and agents to remove toil.

• You can answer customer security questionnaires quickly, accurately and in plain English.

• You can explain a control to an engineer and a risk to an executive, and both come away knowing what to do next.

• You care about the product, and you’ll tell us what’s missing from our own GRC tooling.

• You’re comfortable with high autonomy. Nobody’s going to hand you a detailed spec, you’re trusted to figure out what needs doing and just do it.

• Bonus points for ISO 42001 or AI governance experience, SOC 2, GDPR, or time in a fast-growing SaaS company.

Supporting you
We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

• Private medical insurance. Seriously good cover - we want you and the people you love to be looked after.

• Competitive annual leave. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

• First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

• Enhanced pension. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

• Meaningful equity. We’re rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

• Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We’re all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

• Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we’re doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

• Two budgets that have your back. £1000 to invest in your setup, £500 a year to invest in yourself.

arbeitnow:head-of-research-editorial-lon.description:
About Firstwork
Labour markets are broken. Millions of people are ready to work and can't start. Screening, right-to-work checks, contracts, onboarding and scheduling still run across disconnected systems, with hundreds of manual decisions in between. Firstwork builds AI agents that run frontline workforce operations end to end. We activate hundreds of thousands of workers a month globally for some of the world's largest employers and staffing firms, working forward-deployed inside the customer's operation. Backed by Y Combinator and Gradient (Google’s AI fund), with offices in New York, and London and Dubai opening this year.

Why this role
Frontline labour markets are badly measured. Governments publish unemployment and vacancy statistics. Nobody publishes a credible number for how long it takes to get a qualified person from application to first shift, what that delay costs, or how much of it is regulatory rather than operational.
We see activation at scale, across sectors and jurisdictions, so we can measure what nobody else can. You'll work with partner technical teams and end users to understand what they actually need, then design and build the solution yourself: architecture, implementation, testing, deployment. You'll be close enough to the mission to see why the problem matters, and you'll ship fast, because what you build gets used in the field almost immediately. • Build real working relationships with client technical teams and end users so you understand their problems well enough to solve them properly.

• 4+ years building and shipping production software, in Python and at least one lower-level language (C++, Rust, Go).

• Comfortable owning software end-to-end — design, build, debug, deploy — including on Linux, in operational or field conditions.

• Confident and clear communicating with client technical teams and senior stakeholders, with a bias to action

• Practical under constraint: ill-defined problems, tight deadlines, and a working solution over a theoretically perfect one.

• Travel: frequent on site with partners, domestic and international.

Nice to have

• Prior forward-deployed, solutions engineering, or customer-facing engineering experience.

Today too much of our environmental testing depends on external labs and their scheduling, which slows our development down as much as it costs us. Your mission is to change that, and you own it end to end: defining the capabilities we need, specifying and buying the machines, contributing to the choice of premises, recruiting and leading the technicians, and drawing the line between what we bring in-house and what stays external.

• Define the lab and select the equipment: Establish the capabilities we need, then specify, evaluate and procure the machines, covering climatic and thermal cycling, water and dust ingress, vibration and UV ageing, including a large climate room in which we can fly a drone under controlled wind and temperature.

• Decide what we internalise and what stays external: Draw the line between the tests worth owning and those better bought from external labs, such as accredited qualification or rare capital-heavy tests, and revisit that line as our product range grows.

• Set up the facility: Contribute to the choice of premises, then take the site from layout and utilities through to installation, safety and commissioning.

What we're looking for

• At least 10 years in environmental testing , including setting up or substantially developing a test lab. This is a senior role and we are looking for depth, not a first lab job.

• Strong command of environmental test methods and the equipment behind them: climatic and thermal cycling, vibration, water and dust ingress, UV, and the standards that frame them.

• Proven equipment judgement: able to specify, evaluate and procure test machines, and to argue build-versus-buy and in-house-versus-external on both cost and technical merit.

• Engineering degree in a relevant field (mechanical, materials, electronics, physics or similar), or equivalent experience.

• Bonus: experience with defence or aerospace test standards (MIL-STD-810, RTCA DO-160 or similar); familiarity with lab accreditation and metrological traceability such as ISO/IEC 17025; a background in drones or robotics.

As an FPGA Engineer within our Electronic Warfare team, you will design and implement the real-time digital signal processing that turns raw RF into actionable effect — from receiver channelization and threat detection through to jamming waveform generation. You will own the RTL at the heart of our EW and SIGINT systems, working hand-in-hand with the RF hardware, embedded software and algorithm teams to take a signal chain from concept and simulation to silicon, to the lab, and into the field.

Responsibilities

• RTL Design & Implementation: Design and implement signal-processing datapaths in VHDL or SystemVerilog — digital down-conversion, channelizers, filtering, FFT and detection chains — from specification through to validation.

• Real-Time DSP in Fabric: Implement detection, direction-finding, classification and waveform generation under hard latency and throughput budgets, translating algorithm intent into fixed-point hardware.

• RF & Data Converter Interfacing: Own the digital interface to the RF front-end — high-speed converters (JESD204B/C), multi-channel clocking, synchronization and calibration paths.

• Hardware/Software Partitioning: Define the split between programmable logic and on-chip processors, and the register and streaming interfaces the embedded software team builds against.

• Timing Closure & Resource Budgets: Drive constraints, timing closure, and resource, power and thermal budgets on production hardware.

• Bring-up, Integration & Validation: Lead FPGA bring-up on new boards, bench validation against performance targets with RF instrumentation, and over-the-air testing alongside the systems team.

• Technical Coordination: Collaborate across RF hardware, embedded, GNC and ML teams on system integration and technical interfaces.

• System Reviews & Documentation: Contribute to design and architecture reviews, maintaining consistency between requirements, design and testing.

Candidate Requirements

• Strong RTL design background in VHDL or SystemVerilog for signal-processing datapaths is mandatory.

• Solid digital signal processing fundamentals: sampling, mixing, decimation, filter design, FFT, and fixed-point arithmetic and quantization trade-offs.

• Hands-on experience with SoC FPGAs and their toolchains..

• No prior Electronic Warfare experience required.

• Experience with high-speed data converter interfaces (JESD204B/C) and multi-channel synchronization is a definite plus.

• Experience with algorithm-to-RTL workflows (MATLAB/Simulink, Python modelling, or HLS) is a plus.

• Lab experience with RF instrumentation — spectrum analyzer, vector signal generator, oscilloscope — is a plus.

• MSc in Electrical / Electronics Engineering, Signal Processing or a related field;

• Broad engineering culture with understanding of RF hardware, embedded software and system-level trade-offs.

• Rigorous, structured and mission-driven mindset with strong analytical skills.

• Excellent communication and documentation abilities.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

About the role
Genesis brings together AI research, simulation, and robotics to build general-purpose robots that can work in the real world. Our mission is to unlock unlimited physical labor.
Our ability to grow depends on how well we find exceptional people, hire them, and help them become effective. There are engineering problems throughout that journey: fragmented data, repetitive workflows, disconnected tools, and processes that become slower as the company gets bigger.
You’ll build the software and automations that solve those problems.
Your users will be recruiters, hiring managers, the People team, and employees. You’ll work directly with them, identify the highest-impact opportunities, ship useful tools, and measure what changes. Your work should help us reach stronger candidates, move faster, and give people more time for the decisions and conversations that need them.
What you’ll own

• Building recruiting tools that improve reach and relevance. Create workflows for talent mapping, research, enrichment, and rediscovery of candidates already in our network. Help recruiters turn scattered information into useful context.

• Running measurable growth experiments. Partner with Recruiting to test sourcing channels, outreach workflows, referrals, and candidate nurture. Measure qualified conversations and downstream conversion.

• Connecting our systems. Build integrations across Ashby, our People systems, and collaboration tools using APIs, webhooks, and reliable data pipelines.

• Automating People workflows. Improve onboarding, employee requests, lifecycle handoffs, and recurring reporting. Build tools that make the right action easy and ownership clear.

• Making the data usable. Create trusted datasets and dashboards that show where candidates stall, where teams lose time, and whether a change improves the process.

• Putting AI to practical use. Build and evaluate AI-assisted research, information retrieval, summarization, and workflow support. Make outputs easy to verify and keep people accountable for hiring and employee decisions.

• Owning what you ship. Take tools from prototype to everyday use, with appropriate testing, monitoring, documentation, and access controls. Stay close to users and keep improving them.

You’ll thrive here if

• You’ve built and shipped software, internal tools, or growth systems that people actually use.

• You can code confidently in Python or TypeScript/JavaScript, work with SQL, and integrate APIs.

• You can turn an ambiguous operational problem into a small, useful first version and iterate from there.

• You think in experiments: define the problem, establish a baseline, ship a change, and check the result.

• You’ve built with LLMs and understand how to evaluate output quality and handle failures.

• You care about adoption and reliability as much as the initial build.

• You work well with nontechnical teammates and handle candidate and employee data thoughtfully.

Bonus points

• You’ve worked on recruiting technology, People systems, growth engineering, or revenue operations tooling.

• You’ve built integrations with Ashby or another ATS, CRM, or HRIS.

• You’ve worked with public research and developer data, such as papers, citations, or GitHub profiles.

• You’ve combined custom code with tools such as n8n, Make, or Zapier.

• You’ve been an early builder at a startup and owned tools from initial idea through ongoing maintenance.

The offer

• Competitive base salary plus meaningful equity.

• Visa sponsorship and relocation support.

• Hybrid: 3–4+ days per week in our office.

• A broad engineering remit, direct access to your users, and the opportunity to build systems that help Genesis hire and scale.

Genesis is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome people with different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.

For most people, hotels are places you only visit when you travel.
But we see something different.
Behind their doors, hotels hide some of the most extraordinary spaces cities have to offer: breathtaking rooftops with skyline views, world-class spas and pools, bars and restaurants led by visionary chefs, interiors that spark the imagination, and beds so perfect you never want to leave them.
Yet, most of these spaces remain invisible to the people who live just a few streets away.
Staycation was born from a simple belief: the most inspiring places in your city shouldn’t be reserved for tourists. They should be part of your everyday life, an alternative to a dinner-date at a restaurant, a spontaneous midweek escape, or a unique way to celebrate a special moment.
Our mission is to transform hotels into a new form of urban entertainment.
Places people turn to when they want to feel, connect or recharge. Whether it’s 24 hours, 48 hours, or just a few hours, we’re reinventing the way people experience the cities they call home.
Today, Staycation means:

• 🌍 5 million users in France, the UK, Spain, Belgium and Switzerland

• 🏨 4,000 partner hotels among the best 4★, 5★ and iconic palaces

• ⭐️ 9.3/10 average rating for our experiences

Joining Staycation means becoming part of a passionate, creative, and ambitious team on a quest to redefine what hospitality and city life can be.

✨ The role
We’re hiring a Fullstack Developer to strengthen our Product & Engineering team.
You’ll join one of our cross-functional product squads, working closely with a Lead Developer, a Product Manager, a Product Designer and other Fullstack Developers.
Your role will be to turn user problems into reliable product increments, contribute from discovery to production, and balance impact, speed, quality and maintainability.
We’re open to both experienced and senior individual contributors, and we’ll calibrate the scope based on what you have already owned and delivered. You may be stronger in either frontend or backend, but you should be genuinely comfortable contributing across both and motivated to keep growing on the full stack.
You’ll report to the Lead Developer of your squad and be part of the Product team led by Robin , our CTO & Head of Product.
📍 Key responsibilities

• Design, build, test, deploy and monitor product features across the frontend and backend.

• Work closely with Product Management and Product Design from the problem-definition stage, helping shape the solution rather than simply implementing a finished specification.

• Break down projects into clear increments, estimate your work, identify dependencies and risks, and communicate early when the plan needs to change.

• Take ownership of what you ship in production, from instrumentation and monitoring to incident diagnosis and continuous improvement.

• Contribute to high-quality code reviews, pragmatic testing strategies, refactoring and the active management of technical debt.

• Document decisions, share knowledge and help improve our engineering practices and codebase over time.

• Depending on your level, plan multi-week projects, design architectures that others can implement and introduce practices that continue to work without you in the loop.

🧰 Our tech environment
Four products running on a shared stack:

• The website (React / Next.js), our storefront and booking funnel.

• The mobile app (React Native), used daily by our users, with its own release cycles and performance stakes.

• The hotel extranet , where our partners manage their offers, inventory, bookings, billing, timeslots.

• The internal admin platform , the tool our teams use to run the marketplace.

On the back-end side: micro-services in NestJS and more, PostgreSQL for our databases, hosted on AWS with Terraform.
📌 Key results
In your first 3 months, you’ll be expected to:

• Understand your squad’s product mission, users, metrics and main technical flows.

• Become familiar with our stack, codebase, rituals and path to production.

• Ship a first end-to-end increment and monitor its performance in production.

• Contribute useful code reviews and identify at least one relevant technical risk or improvement.

• Build reliable working relationships with Engineering, Product Management and Product Design.

In your first 12 months, you’ll be expected to:

• Own a meaningful product and technical scope within your squad.

• Have contributed to a measurable product outcome for our users and the business.

• Deliver reliably, surface risks early and make sound trade-offs between speed, quality and reversibility.

• Have improved at least one engineering practice or part of the codebase in a way that benefits the wider team.

• At senior level, have planned and driven a multi-week project or designed an architecture successfully implemented by others.

🌍 Location
This position is open to candidates based anywhere in France , with two possible working arrangements:

• If you are based in the Paris region , you will work in a hybrid setup, with three days per week at our Paris office.

• If you are based elsewhere in France, you can work fully remotely and will join us in Paris for three consecutive days each month (Wednesday to Friday during the first week of the month).

🚀 Why join us?

• Work on a product used by millions of people, with a direct and visible impact on their experience.

• Contribute to ambitious product challenges across the full user journey.

• Own features end to end and take part in product decisions alongside Product and Design.

• Work across web, mobile and backend challenges in an engineering culture that values pragmatism over technical dogma.

• Join a small team with real autonomy, short decision cycles and room to shape the codebase, architecture and ways of working.

• Combine remote flexibility with regular time together as a team in Paris.

🎯 You’re the ideal candidate if you:
Must-haves

• Have at least 5 years of professional software development experience, with a track record of shipping and owning meaningful product features.

• Have real experience contributing to both frontend and backend development, even if one side is currently stronger.

• Have solid experience with React/Next.js or a comparable modern frontend stack , as well as building APIs and working with data using Node.js or a comparable backend stack .

• Have good knowledge of SQL and PostgreSQL .

• Can take a feature from an ambiguous problem to a reliable production release, making pragmatic technical and product trade-offs along the way.

• Care about code quality, testing, maintainability and production reliability without losing sight of delivery and user impact.

• Communicate clearly, collaborate without ego and are comfortable working closely with Product and Design.

• Are autonomous and reliable in a distributed team, while knowing when to ask for context, feedback or support.

Nice-to-haves

• Experience with React Native .

• Experience working on a B2C product, marketplace, mobile application, booking or payment journey.

• Previous experience working remotely.

• Comfortable working in English in a professional environment.

⚙️ Hiring process

• Recruiter interview with Mathieu , our Talent Acquisition Manager (30–45 min)

• Manager interview with Robin , our CTO & Head of Product, and Charlie , one of our Lead Developers (60 min)
